caps.title: Align Series
caps.cap_description: Line several series up on the instants they all have
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Puts two or more series side by side on their shared instants.

## Inputs

- Two or more time series, gathered in the order the machine gives them.

## Outputs

Aligned series: each shared instant with every series' value, in input order.

## Notes

The series are interchangeable items of one list; a machine gathers them: `(a, b, c) -> align-series -> aligned`.

args.name: series
args.arg_description: The series to line up

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: The series on their shared instants

caps.title: Ask (Grounded Question Answering) (Constrained, English)
caps.cap_description: Answer a question over content with verbatim supporting quotes — fabricated evidence is a hard error
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

`cat report.txt | ask --question "what caused the outage?"`: answers strictly from the content, with 1-5 VERBATIM quotes as evidence. The engine VERIFIES every quote actually occurs in the content (whitespace-normalized) — an answer resting on invented evidence is a hard error, never forwarded. When the content does not answer the question, the answer says so with empty quotes and confidence 0.0 — honest absence.

`searchx` finds WHERE; `ask` answers WHAT. Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md).

## Inputs

- The content to answer from (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--question`: the question (required).

## Outputs

A semantic-judgment record: `{"answer": <string>, "quotes": [<verbatim excerpts>], "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "reason": "<how the quotes support the answer>"}`.

## Notes

- Judgments are deterministic (law P4).

args.name: question

caps.title: Bind PDFs
caps.cap_description: Concatenate a sequence of PDFs into a single multi-page PDF
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Stitches a sequence of PDFs into a single multi-page PDF. Each input PDF's pages are appended to the output in arrival order — the first input's pages first, then the second's, and so on. Page contents, resources, and metadata are copied verbatim via pdfium's import-pages path; no re-rendering, no font subsetting, no recompression.

## Inputs

- A sequence of `media:document;ext=pdf` items.

## Outputs

A single `media:document;ext=pdf` whose page count is the sum of all input PDFs' page counts.

## Notes

- Encrypted inputs need `--password`; one password applies to every encrypted input (unencrypted inputs ignore it).

- An empty input sequence is a hard error; an input PDF with zero pages is also a hard error. Both surface the upstream issue rather than silently producing an empty output.
- Each input is loaded as its own pdfium document and its pages are imported into the destination at the running insertion index. Memory usage scales with the size of the largest individual input PDF (loaded one at a time), not with the sum.
- For the inverse (splitting one PDF into per-page PDFs), use [Disbind PDF Into Per-Page PDFs](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:disbind-to-pdf;in="media:document;ext=pdf";out="media:document;ext=pdf").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Sequence of PDF files to concatenate

args.name: password
args.arg_description: Password for encrypted PDFs. Without it, an encrypted PDF fails with an error naming this flag; a wrong password fails saying so.

caps.title: Describe Image (Candle) (Candle (Rust safetensors), ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Generate image descriptions using BLIP models with Candle ML framework
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Generates a natural-language description of a PNG image using BLIP (Bootstrapped Language-Image Pretraining) models running locally via Candle. Suitable for alt-text generation, image indexing, and content moderation pipelines.

## Inputs

- A PNG image file.
- An optional caption PREFIX the model continues (BLIP conditional captioning, e.g. "a photograph of") — BLIP is a captioner, not an instruction-follower, so the prompt is not a question or instruction. Without a prompt, BLIP produces a general caption.
- An optional maximum caption length in tokens (default 256).
- A BLIP model spec from HuggingFace. Defaults to `Salesforce/blip-image-captioning-large`, the Candle vision model in the offline travel kit.

## Outputs

A text description of the image as a plain string.

## Notes

- BLIP models produce shorter, more caption-like descriptions than vision-language models (LLaVA/Qwen). For detailed, instruction-following descriptions, prefer [Describe Image (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:describe-image;gguf;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text";vision) or [Describe Image (MLX)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:describe-image;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;mlx;out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text";vision).
- Input must be PNG. An image in another format is converted first with [Convert Image Format](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-image;in=media:image;out=media:image); a machine planned from a JPEG or WebP source takes that step by itself.
- For embedding an image into a vector space rather than describing it, use [Generate Image Embeddings (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:generate-image-embeddings;candle;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;out="media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the image file to describe

args.name: prompt
args.arg_description: Optional caption PREFIX the model continues (BLIP conditional captioning, e.g. "a photograph of") — not an instruction. Omit for unconditional captioning.

args.name: max-tokens
args.arg_description: Maximum caption length in tokens

args.name: system-prompt
args.arg_description: System prompt that frames the model's behaviour for the request. Applied via the model's chat template when the downloaded VLM carries one (chat-template-jinja or chat-template-short); dropped for base/completion vision models such as BLIP. Default is a generic helpful-assistant frame; concrete per-image instructions belong in the prompt slot.
args.default_value: You are a helpful assistant. Respond to the user's input with a useful, accurate, and concise reply. If the input is a document or excerpt, treat it as the subject of the user's request and respond about it.

args.name: model
args.arg_description: BLIP model name from HuggingFace

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Generated text description of the image

caps.title: Get Embeddings Dimensions (Candle) (Candle (Rust safetensors), ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Query the dimensionality of embeddings for a given Candle model
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Reports the vector size that a Candle-based embedding model produces. Use this before creating a vector index so you know how many dimensions to allocate.

## Inputs

- A model spec pointing to a HuggingFace BERT-architecture embedding model. Defaults to `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, the Candle embeddings model in the offline travel kit.

## Outputs

A single integer: the number of dimensions in each embedding vector this model produces.

## Notes

- The result is read from the model's saved configuration, not from running inference, so it is fast and requires no GPU memory.
- Use at pipeline setup time to parameterize downstream vector store caps.
- See also: [Generate Vector Embeddings (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:candle;generate-embeddings;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";ml-model;out="media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record")

args.name: input
args.arg_description: HuggingFace model name to query dimensions for

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

caps.title: Generate Vector Embeddings (Candle) (Candle (Rust safetensors), ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Generate vector embeddings from text using Candle ML framework on CPU/GPU
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Encodes text into dense floating-point vectors suitable for semantic search, clustering, classification, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Uses sentence-transformers models running locally via Candle on CPU or GPU. Long documents are automatically split into overlapping chunks; each chunk gets its own vector.

## Inputs

- A text file to embed.
- A model spec (HuggingFace BERT-architecture repo). Defaults to `sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, the Candle embeddings model in the offline travel kit.
- Chunk size in words (default 400) and chunk overlap in words (default 50). Adjust to match your retrieval granularity.

## Outputs

A JSON record containing an array of embedding objects. Each object includes the chunk text, its position in the document, the embedding vector (array of floats), and model metadata (model name, dimensions).

## Notes

- Choose chunk size based on context: smaller chunks (100-200 words) give precise retrieval; larger chunks (500-800 words) give more context per match.
- Overlap prevents important content from being cut across chunk boundaries.
- A chunk whose tokenization exceeds the model's positional capacity (512 tokens for MiniLM-class models) is embedded window-by-window and the window embeddings are mean-pooled weighted by token count, then L2-normalized — the whole chunk always contributes; nothing is rejected or silently truncated.
- Candle supports both CPU and CUDA GPU. GPU significantly reduces latency for large documents.
- Use [Get Embeddings Dimensions (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:embeddings-dimensions;candle;in="media:candle;embeddings;enc=utf8;model-spec;repo-safetensors;tokenizer-unified";ml-model;out="media:integer;model-dim;numeric") to check the vector size before building an index.
- For GGUF-quantized models, see [Generate Vector Embeddings (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:generate-embeddings;gguf;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";ml-model;out="media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to text file to generate embeddings from

args.name: model
args.arg_description: HuggingFace model name for embeddings

args.name: chunk-size
args.arg_description: Chunk size in words for splitting input text

args.name: chunk-overlap
args.arg_description: Chunk overlap in words when splitting input text

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON containing embeddings, chunk metadata and model information

caps.title: Generate Image Embeddings (Candle) (Candle (Rust safetensors), ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Generate image embeddings using CLIP models with Candle ML framework
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Encodes a PNG image into a dense floating-point vector using CLIP (Contrastive Language-Image Pretraining). The resulting vector lives in the same semantic space as CLIP text embeddings, enabling cross-modal similarity search — find images by text queries and vice versa.

## Inputs

- A PNG image file.
- A CLIP-architecture model spec from HuggingFace. Defaults to `openai/clip-vit-base-patch32`, the image-embeddings model in the offline travel kit.

## Outputs

A JSON record containing the image embedding vector and model metadata.

## Notes

- CLIP image and text vectors are compatible: you can compare an image embedding to text embeddings generated by a CLIP text encoder in the same vector space.
- Input must be PNG. An image in another format is converted first with [Convert Image Format](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-image;in=media:image;out=media:image); a machine planned from a JPEG or WebP source takes that step by itself.
- For describing image content in natural language rather than embedding it, use [Describe Image (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:describe-image;candle;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the image file to embed

args.name: model
args.arg_description: CLIP-architecture model name from HuggingFace

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Image embedding vector with model metadata

caps.title: Generate Text with LLM (Candle) (Candle (Rust safetensors), LLM, ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Generate text using Candle transformer models (multi-architecture safetensors).
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Accepts a raw text prompt and generates a text continuation using a Candle safetensors LLM. This is a simpler, prompt-in / text-out interface compared to the structured request used by the llm-inference caps. Suitable for quick text generation without building a full generation request object.

## Inputs

- A text prompt (plain text, passed via stdin or positional arg).
- A model spec (HuggingFace safetensors repo). Defaults to `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct`, the Candle LLM in the offline travel kit.
- Sampling parameters: max tokens (512), temperature (0.7), top-p (0.9), seed (42).
- Optional HuggingFace bearer token (`hf_token`) for gated repositories — required for `gemma`, `gemma2`, `gemma3` and any other licence-protected model.

## Outputs

Generated text streamed as raw text chunks (not NDJSON).

## Notes

- Architectures supported: mistral, llama, qwen2, qwen3, phi, phi3, gemma, gemma2, gemma3, falcon, olmo, olmo2. The architecture is detected from the model's `config.json` `model_type` — pickers driven by `supported_model_types` will reject any model whose architecture is outside this list. Yi is unsupported in this cap because `candle-transformers` 0.9.2 ships a non-deserialisable `yi::Config`; use the GGUF or MLX backends for Yi.
- For structured output, system prompts, or streaming JSON events, use [LLM Text Generation (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:llm-inference;candle;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-generation-request;record";llm;ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream") instead.
- Requires safetensors model weights (not GGUF).
- Gated repositories require `hf_token`. Without one, the call fails hard with a clear authentication error rather than silently downgrading.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Input text prompt for generation

args.name: system-prompt
args.arg_description: System prompt that frames the model's behaviour for the request. Applied via the model's chat template when the downloaded model carries one (chat-template-jinja or chat-template-short); ignored for base/completion models. Default is a generic helpful-assistant frame that works for arbitrary user input — task-specific prompts (summarise, translate, explain) belong in the user-message slot.
args.default_value: You are a helpful assistant. Respond to the user's input with a useful, accurate, and concise reply. If the input is a document or excerpt, treat it as the subject of the user's request and respond about it.

args.name: model-spec
args.arg_description: Candle model specification (HuggingFace repo with safetensors weights and a unified tokenizer.json)

args.name: hf-token
args.arg_description: HuggingFace bearer token. Required when targeting a gated repository (license-protected models). Without it, gated downloads fail with a clear authentication error.

args.name: max-tokens
args.arg_description: Maximum number of tokens to generate

args.name: temperature
args.arg_description: Sampling temperature (0.0-2.0)

args.name: top-p
args.arg_description: Top-p (nucleus) sampling parameter

args.name: seed
args.arg_description: Random seed for reproducibility

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Generated text streamed as raw text chunks

caps.title: Transcribe Audio (Candle) (Candle (Rust safetensors), ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Transcribe audio files to text using Whisper models with Candle ML framework
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Converts spoken audio into text using OpenAI Whisper models running locally via the Candle ML framework. Runs on CPU or GPU without a network dependency after the model is downloaded.

## Inputs

- A WAV audio stream (mono or stereo, any sample rate Whisper supports) — a bounded file, or the UNBOUNDED streaming WAV a live microphone machine produces via `encode-audio-frames-wav`. Non-speech audio simply yields little or no text.
- An optional language code (e.g. `en`, `fr`, `zh`). Omit to let Whisper auto-detect the language.
- Every emitted record carries its window start/end times (window-level boundaries, not token-level timestamps) — there is no timestamps flag to forget.
- An optional model spec pointing to a HuggingFace Whisper checkpoint. Defaults to `openai/whisper-base`, the offline-travel-kit transcription model.

## Outputs

A SEQUENCE of JSON transcription records, one per 30-second Whisper window, each carrying the window's text, its start/end times, the detected language, and the model name. Over a live microphone the records stream out as each window fills — live transcription — and the sequence ends when the feed stops. Over a bounded file the same per-window records arrive as they are transcribed.

## Notes

- Larger Whisper models (`whisper-small`, `whisper-medium`, `whisper-large-v3`) produce more accurate transcripts at the cost of memory and latency.
- Input must be WAV. Convert other audio formats upstream before passing to this cap; live microphone capture arrives via `encode-audio-frames-wav` (the planner inserts it automatically for `media:audio;live;microphone` sources).
- Audio of any length is transcribed in full: it is processed in Whisper's native 30-second windows and the window transcripts are concatenated in order. Nothing is truncated.
- See also: [Generate Vector Embeddings (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:candle;generate-embeddings;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";ml-model;out="media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") to embed the resulting transcript.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the audio file (WAV format)

args.name: language
args.arg_description: Language code for transcription (e.g. en, fr, zh). Omit to auto-detect on multilingual models; English-only checkpoints accept only en.

args.name: model
args.arg_description: Whisper model name from HuggingFace

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Transcribed text with optional timestamps and metadata

caps.title: LLM Text Generation (Candle) (Candle (Rust safetensors), LLM, ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Generate text using Candle transformer models. Output is NDJSON streaming tokens.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Runs autoregressive text generation using Candle transformer models (safetensors format). Accepts a fully-structured generation request and streams output as NDJSON tokens. This is the low-level inference cap used by higher-level caps like Summarize and Generate Code.

## Inputs

A single JSON generation request record containing: the prompt, model spec (HuggingFace safetensors repo), sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, max tokens, seed), and an optional system prompt.

Optional HuggingFace bearer token (`hf_token`) for gated repositories — required for `gemma`, `gemma2`, `gemma3` and any other licence-protected model.

## Outputs

An NDJSON stream. Each line is a JSON object. Lines carry token text, status events (`started`, `complete`), and a final summary with total tokens and timing.

## Notes

- Every execution is streaming — there is no non-streaming mode.
- Candle runs on CPU, Metal, or CUDA. GPU is strongly recommended for models larger than 3B parameters.
- Architectures supported: mistral, llama, qwen2, qwen3, phi, phi3, gemma, gemma2, gemma3, falcon, olmo, olmo2. The architecture is detected from the model's `config.json` `model_type` — pickers driven by `supported_model_types` will reject any model whose architecture is outside this list. Yi is unsupported in this cap because `candle-transformers` 0.9.2 ships a non-deserialisable `yi::Config`; use the GGUF or MLX backends for Yi.
- For higher-level tasks (summarization, code generation, creative writing), use the task-specific inference caps rather than this one directly.
- For constrained output (JSON schema, regex), use [Constrained LLM Generation (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:llm-inference-constrained;constrained;gguf;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-generation-request;record";llm;ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: The generation request containing prompt, model spec, and parameters

args.name: hf-token
args.arg_description: HuggingFace bearer token. Required when targeting a gated repository (license-protected models). Without it, gated downloads fail with a clear authentication error.

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: NDJSON stream of tokens, status updates, and completion message

caps.title: Change Series
caps.cap_description: Measure how a series changes: in percent, as a log ratio or as a difference, over so many observations
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Turns a series into its changes: each value compared with the one `over` observations before it.

## Inputs

- A time series.
- `how`: percent, log or difference.
- `over`: how many observations back.

## Outputs

A time series of the changes, starting `over` observations in.

## Notes

A percent or log change from zero or below is refused for that instant and counted; a series with no instant left is refused.

caps.title: Classify (Closed-Set Labeling) (Constrained, English)
caps.cap_description: Classify an item into exactly one of N allowed labels, with confidence and rationale
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

The semantic router's workhorse: puts an item into exactly one of the labels you allow. `cat emails.ndjson | classify --labels urgent,billing,spam,personal` per item. The label is token-level constrained to the allowed set — a hallucinated label is impossible by construction.

Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md).

## Inputs

- The item to classify (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--labels`: 2-64 allowed labels, comma- or newline-separated, no duplicates (violations are hard errors naming the rule).
- An optional `--context` framing what the labels mean here.

## Outputs

A semantic-judgment record: `{"label": <one of the allowed labels>, "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "reason": "<one sentence>"}`.

## Notes

- Judgments are deterministic (law P4): same item, labels, and model produce the same label.

caps.cap_description: Parse a string value as an integer
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Parses a text string as an integer. Use this when a string-producing cap outputs a number as text (e.g. from a file or LLM output) and a downstream cap requires an integer type.

## Inputs

A UTF-8 text string value representing an integer (media type `media:enc=utf8`).

The parsed integer.

caps.title: Coerce String to Boolean
caps.cap_description: Convert a string value to a boolean
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a string media value to a boolean (`true` / `false`). The missing inverse of the boolean→* coercion family: use it when a downstream cap requires a boolean but the upstream cap produces a string.

## Inputs

A string value (media type `media:enc=utf8`).

## Outputs

The boolean `true` or `false`.

## Notes

- Strict accepted spellings, nothing else: `true`/`false`, `1`/`0`, `yes`/`no`, `on`/`off` (case-insensitive, whitespace-trimmed). Anything outside that set is a hard error naming the accepted values — "truthiness" of arbitrary values would be a silent guess.
- This is a type-level adapter for the capfab planner, like the rest of the coerce family.

caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Parses a text string as a floating-point number. Use this when a string-producing cap outputs a numeric value as text and a downstream cap requires a numeric type.

## Inputs

A UTF-8 text string representing a number (media type `media:enc=utf8`).

## Outputs

The parsed floating-point number.

## Notes

- Fails hard if the string is not a valid numeric value.
- For integers specifically, use [Coerce String to Integer](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:enc=utf8";out="media:integer;numeric").
- For the reverse, use [Coerce Number to String](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:coerce;in="media:numeric";out="media:enc=utf8").

caps.title: Collect JSON Objects into CSV
caps.cap_description: Collect individual JSON objects into a single CSV file
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Gathers a sequence of individual JSON objects into a single CSV file. Object keys become column headers; one row is written per object. Use this to produce tabular output from a fan-in of JSON-producing parallel stages.

## Inputs

A sequence of JSON record objects.

## Outputs

A CSV file with headers derived from the union of all object keys, and one row per object.

## Notes

- Objects with missing keys produce empty cells in those columns.
- Objects with different key sets are merged into a unified column set.
- For a JSON array output instead, use [Collect JSON Objects into Array](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-json-objects;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;!list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record").

caps.title: Collect JSON Objects into Array
caps.cap_description: Collect individual JSON objects into a single JSON array
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Gathers a sequence of individual JSON objects (one per pipeline item) into a single JSON array. Use this to fan-in results from parallel processing where each parallel branch produces one JSON object.

## Inputs

A sequence of JSON record objects.

## Outputs

A JSON array containing all input objects in order.

## Notes

- The objects do not need to have the same keys; heterogeneous objects are permitted.
- For CSV output, use [Collect JSON Objects into CSV](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-json-objects;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;!list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record").
- For YAML output, use [Collect JSON Objects into YAML List](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-json-objects;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;!list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml;list;record").

## Inputs

A sequence of JSON record objects.

A YAML sequence where each element is a mapping corresponding to one input JSON object.

## Notes

- Key order in the YAML output may differ from the JSON input; YAML mappings are unordered by spec.
- For a JSON array output, use [Collect JSON Objects into Array](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-json-objects;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;!list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record").

caps.title: Merge CSV Files
caps.cap_description: Merge multiple CSV files into a single CSV file
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Merges a sequence of CSV files into a single CSV file. Headers from the first file are used; subsequent files contribute their data rows. Use this to fan-in results from parallel processing stages that each produce a CSV.

## Inputs

A sequence of CSV files (each with a header row and one or more data rows).

## Outputs

A single merged CSV file containing all rows from all inputs, with a single header.

## Notes

- All input CSVs must have compatible headers (same columns in the same order).
- Output preserves the row order of the inputs (first input rows appear first).
- For cross-format merging (CSV inputs to JSON or YAML output), use [Merge CSV Files into JSON Array](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record") or [Merge CSV Files into YAML List](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:collect-records;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml;list;record").

caps.title: Concat Text
caps.cap_description: Concatenate a sequence of text items into a single text value
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Stitches a sequence of text items into one text value, with an optional separator inserted between adjacent items. The bare `media:enc=utf8` input subsumes any concrete text variant — txt, md, rst, log, JSON-as-text — so the planner routes them all through this cap.

## Inputs

- A sequence of text items.
- An optional `--separator` string (default: `"\n"`).

## Outputs

A single text value whose value is `items[0] + sep + items[1] + sep + … + items[N-1]`.

## Notes

- The output URN is bare `media:enc=utf8` because the merged result no longer carries any single input's format-specific tags. Pipelines that need format-specific concatenation (e.g. preserving `media:enc=utf8;ext=md;plain-text`) should produce per-format variants.
- Separator UTF-8 must be valid; non-UTF-8 bytes fail loudly.
- An empty input sequence is a hard error — silently emitting `""` would let downstream caps run on nothing without surfacing the upstream sequence being empty.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Sequence of text items to concatenate

args.name: separator
args.arg_description: String inserted between adjacent items (default: newline)

caps.title: Explain (Root-Cause Hypothesis) (Constrained, English)
caps.cap_description: Explain opaque data (logs, errors, configs) against a goal, with verified verbatim evidence and next checks
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

`cat crash.log | explain --goal "find likely root cause"`: forms the most likely hypothesis serving the goal, cites 1-5 VERBATIM excerpts from the data as evidence, and proposes up to 3 concrete next checks. The engine VERIFIES every evidence excerpt actually occurs in the data — an explanation that cannot point at real evidence is a guess, and a fabricated citation is a hard error.

Built for logs; works on configs, stack traces, and other opaque artifacts. Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md).

## Inputs

- The data to explain (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--goal`: what the explanation is for (required).

## Outputs

A semantic-judgment record: `{"hypothesis": <string>, "evidence": [<verified verbatim excerpts>], "next_checks": [<concrete checks>], "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "reason": "<why this hypothesis beats the alternatives>"}`.

## Notes

- Judgments are deterministic (law P4).

args.arg_description: The opaque data to explain

args.name: goal

caps.title: Extract (Schema-Guided Extraction) (Constrained, English)
caps.cap_description: Extract structured fields from messy content into a caller-supplied JSON schema, wrapped in the judgment envelope
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

`cat invoice.txt | extract --schema invoice.schema.json`: pulls the fields your schema describes out of messy content. The judgment-envelope generalization of [Generate JSON](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:constrained;generate-json;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";language=en;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;record"): the extracted instance lands in the envelope's `result` field, so extraction confidence and ambiguity notes are first-class — and the WHOLE response (instance and envelope) is token-level constrained.

Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md).

## Inputs

- The content to extract from (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--schema`: the JSON Schema the `result` field must validate against.

## Outputs

A semantic-judgment record: `{"result": <instance matching your schema>, "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "reason": "<anything ambiguous or missing>"}`.

## Notes

- Extraction is faithful by contract: only what the content states is extracted — absent values are omitted or null where the schema permits, never invented.
- Judgments are deterministic (law P4).

caps.title: Generate JSON (Constrained, English)
caps.cap_description: Generate JSON from text content, constrained to validate against a caller-supplied JSON schema.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Runs constrained LLM generation over the supplied content to produce a JSON
object that validates against the supplied JSON schema. Token-level schema
enforcement (via LLGuidance on the GGUF backend) guarantees the output parses
and satisfies the schema — downstream code can `serde_json::from_str::<T>` or
its equivalent without defensive error handling.

## Inputs

- Content to analyze — plain text (the cap's stdin-flowing input).
- `--schema`: a JSON Schema object describing the required output shape.
- Language code (default: `en`).
- A model spec (defaults to `unsloth/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF` Q4_K_M, the smallest model that answered every judgment test correctly).

## Outputs

A JSON object conforming to the supplied schema.

## Notes

- The output schema is supplied per-call, not looked up from any registry.
  Callers who want a fixed-shape "named query" endpoint should define their
  own cap that wraps this one with a baked-in schema.
- Constraint enforcement is at the token-sampling level — the model cannot
  emit tokens that would violate the schema.
- See also: [Make a Decision](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:constrained;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";language=en;make-decision;out="media:decision;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record")
  and [Make Multiple Decisions](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:constrained;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";language=en;make-multiple-decisions;out="media:decision;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record")
  for fixed-shape boolean classification caps.

caps.title: Constrained LLM Generation (GGUF) (ML Model, GGUF (llama.cpp), LLM, Constrained)
caps.cap_description: Generate text with LLGuidance constraints (JSON schema, regex, grammar). Output is NDJSON streaming.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Runs autoregressive text generation with hard structural constraints using LLGuidance. The model is guaranteed to produce output that matches the supplied JSON schema, regular expression, or grammar — making this the right cap when downstream code must parse the LLM output without error handling for malformed text.

## Inputs

A JSON generation request record that additionally includes a `constraint` field. The constraint can be one of:
- `json_schema`: a JSON Schema object the output must validate against
- `regex`: a regular expression string the output must match
- `grammar`: a context-free grammar in GBNF or LLGuidance format

## Outputs

An NDJSON stream of constrained tokens and a final completion message, same format as the unconstrained inference caps.

## Notes

- Constraint enforcement happens at the token-sampling level via LLGuidance — the model cannot produce tokens that would violate the constraint.
- Structured output via JSON schema is the most common use case: specify the exact fields and types you need and receive valid JSON every time.
- Performance overhead compared to unconstrained inference is small for simple schemas; complex grammars may add latency.
- Use this cap when building pipelines where a downstream cap expects well-formed JSON and you cannot tolerate parse failures.
- See also: [Make a Decision](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:constrained;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";language=en;make-decision;out="media:decision;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") and [Generate JSON](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:constrained;generate-json;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";language=en;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") for higher-level constrained tasks.

caps.title: Make a Decision (Constrained, English)
caps.cap_description: Make a single binary (yes/no, true/false) decision based on content and a question
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Classifies content against a single yes/no question using constrained LLM generation, guaranteeing a structured JSON boolean output. Use this for routing, filtering, and classification steps in pipelines where downstream code expects a machine-readable true/false value.

## Inputs

- Content to analyze (text).
- A binary question about that content (e.g. "Does this document contain personally identifiable information?").
- Language code (default: `en`).
- An optional content-length bound (default 0 = whole content; the backend auto-sizes its context window to the prompt, so nothing needs to "fit").
- Confidence threshold (default 0.7) — decisions below this threshold may be flagged.
- A model spec (defaults to `unsloth/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF` Q4_K_M, the smallest model that answered every judgment test correctly).

## Outputs

A JSON record with a `value` boolean field and a confidence score.

## Notes

- Output is guaranteed to be valid JSON (via LLGuidance constraint) — no parsing of free-form text required.
- For multiple simultaneous questions against the same content, use [Make Multiple Decisions](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:constrained;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";language=en;make-multiple-decisions;out="media:decision;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") to avoid redundant model loads.
- For decisions with natural-language explanations, run an LLM-inference cap directly (the `inference-*-en` orchestrator caps were removed; use `cap:llm-text-generation-*` plus your own prompt).

caps.title: Make Multiple Decisions (Constrained, English)
caps.cap_description: Make multiple binary (yes/no, true/false) decisions based on content and multiple questions
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Classifies content against multiple yes/no questions in a single model call using constrained LLM generation. More efficient than calling [Make a Decision](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:constrained;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";language=en;make-decision;out="media:decision;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") repeatedly when you have several questions about the same document.

## Inputs

- Content to analyze (text).
- A sequence of binary questions (one per line, passed as a multi-value argument). All questions are evaluated against the same content in one inference pass.
- Language code (default: `en`).
- An optional content-length bound (default 0 = whole content).
- Confidence threshold (default 0.7).
- A model spec (defaults to `unsloth/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-GGUF` Q4_K_M, the smallest model that answered every judgment test correctly).

## Outputs

A sequence of JSON records, one per question, each containing a question identifier and a boolean `value`.

## Notes

- Output order matches the input question order.
- All questions share the same content context in a single inference call, which is significantly more efficient than one call per question.
- Output is guaranteed structured JSON via LLGuidance constraint.

caps.title: Normalize (Entity Canonicalization) (Constrained, English)
caps.cap_description: Canonicalize a messy real-world entity value, with confidence and rationale
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Canonicalizes messy real-world values: dates to RFC 3339, phone numbers to E.164, companies to registered names, people to "Given Family", addresses to one comma-separated line, units to SI. Canonicalization reformats — it never drops identifying information. A value that cannot be read as the requested type at all comes back with an empty canonical form and confidence 0.0, with the reason naming what is wrong — visible failure, never a guess.

Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md).

## Inputs

- The value to normalize (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--type`: the entity kind (company, person, date, address, unit, phone, ...).
- An optional `--locale` (BCP 47, e.g. `it-IT`) for locale-dependent values like numeric dates.

## Outputs

A semantic-judgment record: `{"canonical": <the canonical form>, "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "reason": "<one sentence>"}`.

## Notes

- Judgments are deterministic (law P4).

caps.documentation:
## Purpose

`cat thread.txt | summarize --for "decide next action"`: compression judged by whether the reader can act on it, not by coverage. The purpose is REQUIRED — a summary without a purpose is lossy in unknown ways; making the purpose mandatory is what turns this from a chatbot verb into a tool.

Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md). Unlike the judgment caps, the output is the summary text itself (finalised plain text); the model's confidence and its note on what was deliberately dropped are logged.

## Inputs

- The content to summarize (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--for`: the purpose the summary serves (required).
- An optional `--budget`: maximum length in words.

## Outputs

The summary as plain text.

## Notes

- An empty summary is a hard error carrying the model's reason — never an empty artifact.

caps.title: Same (Semantic Equivalence) (Constrained, English)
caps.cap_description: Judge whether two items refer to the same thing, with confidence and rationale
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

The semantic `cmp`: decides whether two items refer to the same real-world thing — not whether they are textually equal. `same --context "company names in invoices" "OpenAI LLC" "Open AI"` returns `{"same": true, "confidence": 0.94, "reason": "spacing/legal suffix variation"}`. Use it in loops and joins wherever fuzzy identity matters: entity deduplication, record matching, reconciliation.

The first of the semantic-primitive cap family (see docs/semantic-primitives.md): Unix-style stdin→transform→stdout tools whose transform is a machine judgment with a guaranteed structured shape.

## Inputs

- The first item (stdin or first positional argument).
- The second item (second positional argument).
- An optional `--context` framing what "the same" means here (e.g. "company names on invoices"). One sentence; it configures the judgment, it is not a conversation.
- A model spec (defaults to the offline-travel-kit GGUF LLM).

## Outputs

A semantic-judgment record: `{"same": <bool>, "confidence": <0.0-1.0>, "reason": "<one sentence>"}`. The shape is guaranteed by token-level constrained generation (LLGuidance) — downstream code parses it without error handling for malformed text.

## Notes

- Judgment caps are deterministic by default (temperature 0 semantics at the backend; law P4 in the design doc): the same items, context, and model produce the same judgment.
- Spelling variants, abbreviations, legal suffixes, and formatting differences do not make two references to one thing different; two genuinely different things are not the same however similar they look. The `reason` field names the decisive evidence.
- Served by the engine's generative-text cartridge over constrained GGUF inference (like [Make a Decision](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:constrained;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";language=en;make-decision;out="media:decision;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record")).

caps.title: Convert AAC to FLAC
caps.cap_description: Decode AAC (ADTS) and re-encode as lossless FLAC
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes a raw AAC (ADTS-framed) file and writes it as FLAC.

## Inputs

An AAC file in ADTS framing.

## Outputs

A FLAC file. Bit depth is preserved up to FLAC's 24-bit cap: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as 16-bit FLAC, 17-24-bit as 24-bit FLAC (both lossless); wider-than-24-bit and float sources reduce to 24-bit WITH triangular dithering (a stated depth reduction, never a silent truncation).

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the AAC file to convert

caps.title: Convert AAC to WAV
caps.cap_description: Decode AAC (ADTS) to uncompressed WAV (PCM)
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes a raw AAC (ADTS-framed) file and writes it as PCM WAV (bit depth preserved from the source).

## Inputs

An AAC file in ADTS framing. AAC tracks inside MP4 containers should use the M4A converter.

## Outputs

A PCM WAV file. PCM WAV preserving the source's bit depth: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as pcm_s16le, 17-24-bit as pcm_s24le, wider integer as pcm_s32le, float sources as pcm_f32le — all lossless, nothing is truncated.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the AAC file to convert

## Purpose

Decodes an AIFF file and writes it as FLAC. Both are lossless; FLAC is dramatically smaller.

## Inputs

An AIFF file. AIFF-C with PCM payload is supported.

## Outputs

A FLAC file. Bit depth is preserved up to FLAC's 24-bit cap: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as 16-bit FLAC, 17-24-bit as 24-bit FLAC (both lossless); wider-than-24-bit and float sources reduce to 24-bit WITH triangular dithering (a stated depth reduction, never a silent truncation).

caps.title: Convert AIFF to WAV
caps.cap_description: Decode an AIFF file to uncompressed WAV (PCM)
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes an AIFF (Audio Interchange File Format) file and writes it as PCM WAV (bit depth preserved from the source). AIFF and WAV are both PCM containers; this is a re-container.

## Inputs

An AIFF file. AIFF-C with PCM payload is supported. AIFF-C with compressed payloads is not.

## Outputs

A PCM WAV file. PCM WAV preserving the source's bit depth: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as pcm_s16le, 17-24-bit as pcm_s24le, wider integer as pcm_s32le, float sources as pcm_f32le — all lossless, nothing is truncated.

A PCM WAV file. PCM WAV preserving the source's bit depth: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as pcm_s16le, 17-24-bit as pcm_s24le, wider integer as pcm_s32le, float sources as pcm_f32le — all lossless, nothing is truncated.

caps.title: Convert M4A to FLAC
caps.cap_description: Decode an M4A (AAC-in-MP4) file and re-encode as lossless FLAC
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Demuxes the audio track from an M4A container, decodes the AAC bitstream, and writes it as FLAC.

## Inputs

An M4A file. AAC and ALAC tracks are supported.

## Outputs

A FLAC file. Bit depth is preserved up to FLAC's 24-bit cap: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as 16-bit FLAC, 17-24-bit as 24-bit FLAC (both lossless); wider-than-24-bit and float sources reduce to 24-bit WITH triangular dithering (a stated depth reduction, never a silent truncation).

Demuxes the audio track from an M4A container and decodes the AAC (or ALAC) bitstream as PCM WAV (bit depth preserved from the source).

## Inputs

An M4A file. AAC and Apple Lossless (ALAC) audio tracks are supported.

## Outputs

A PCM WAV file at the source's native sample rate and channel count. PCM WAV preserving the source's bit depth: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as pcm_s16le, 17-24-bit as pcm_s24le, wider integer as pcm_s32le, float sources as pcm_f32le — all lossless, nothing is truncated.

caps.title: Convert MP3 to FLAC
caps.cap_description: Decode MP3 and re-encode as lossless FLAC
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes an MP3 file and writes it as FLAC. Useful for archiving the decoded MP3 without further generation loss.

## Inputs

An MP3 file.

## Outputs

A FLAC file containing the decoded PCM exactly as the MP3 decoder produced it. Bit depth is preserved up to FLAC's 24-bit cap: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as 16-bit FLAC, 17-24-bit as 24-bit FLAC (both lossless); wider-than-24-bit and float sources reduce to 24-bit WITH triangular dithering (a stated depth reduction, never a silent truncation).

## Notes

The output preserves the MP3 decoder's PCM exactly; no further lossy compression is applied.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the MP3 file to convert

caps.title: Convert MP3 to WAV
caps.cap_description: Decode MP3 to uncompressed WAV (PCM)
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes an MP3 file and writes it as PCM WAV (bit depth preserved from the source). This is the canonical step before transcription, since [Transcribe Audio (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:candle;in="media:audio;ext=wav";ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;record;transcript";transcribe) requires WAV input.

## Inputs

An MP3 file (CBR or VBR, any sample rate or channel count Symphonia supports).

## Outputs

A PCM WAV file at the source's native sample rate and channel count. PCM WAV preserving the source's bit depth: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as pcm_s16le, 17-24-bit as pcm_s24le, wider integer as pcm_s32le, float sources as pcm_f32le — all lossless, nothing is truncated.

## Notes

The output is bit-exact decoded PCM; no resampling is performed. If a downstream consumer requires a specific sample rate, follow with a resampling cap.

caps.title: Convert Opus to FLAC
caps.cap_description: Decode Opus and re-encode as FLAC
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes an Opus audio file (typically wrapped in an Ogg container) and writes the resulting PCM as a FLAC file.

## Inputs

An Opus file.

## Outputs

A FLAC file containing the decoded PCM as produced by the Opus decoder at 48 kHz. Bit depth is preserved up to FLAC's 24-bit cap: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as 16-bit FLAC, 17-24-bit as 24-bit FLAC (both lossless); wider-than-24-bit and float sources reduce to 24-bit WITH triangular dithering (a stated depth reduction, never a silent truncation).

## Notes

Opus always decodes to 48 kHz PCM internally. The FLAC output therefore reports a 48 kHz sample rate regardless of the encoder hint embedded in the OpusHead identification packet.

A PCM WAV file at 48 kHz (Opus's native rate). PCM WAV preserving the source's bit depth: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as pcm_s16le, 17-24-bit as pcm_s24le, wider integer as pcm_s32le, float sources as pcm_f32le — all lossless, nothing is truncated.

Bit depth is preserved up to FLAC's 24-bit cap: 16-bit-or-less sources encode as 16-bit FLAC, 17-24-bit as 24-bit FLAC (both lossless); wider-than-24-bit and float sources reduce to 24-bit WITH triangular dithering (a stated depth reduction, never a silent truncation).

caps.title: Convert Audio Format
caps.cap_description: Re-encode an audio file from one format to another. Abstract: the concrete per-format cap is selected from the input file's type and the requested target.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

The generic form of the per-format audio converters (e.g. [Convert MP3 to WAV](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-audio;in="media:audio;ext=mp3";out="media:audio;ext=wav")). It is **abstract**: it names the operation (`convert-audio`) and says both sides are [audio](https://capdag.com/browse/media:audio), without pinning either format.

Running `convert-audio <file> --to <format>` detects the input's media type, then narrows to the concrete converter for that source/target pair. Because an audio file can usually convert to more than one target, a target is required when the input alone is ambiguous — pass `--to wav` (or `--to flac`, etc.). A file that is not audio is refused as such, and so is a target that is not an audio format. It is never backed by a cartridge directly and never appears as a runnable edge in the cap graph; it is a dispatch umbrella and an alias target only.

## Inputs

Any audio file whose format a concrete `convert-audio` cap implements.

## Outputs

The same audio re-encoded in the requested target format.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the audio file to convert

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: The re-encoded audio in the requested target format.

caps.title: Convert JSON to YAML
caps.cap_description: Re-serialize any JSON value as YAML, keeping its shape
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Re-serializes any JSON value as YAML: a scalar, a list, a record or a list of records. The value's structure, and every marker that describes it (`list`, `record`, a named record such as `model-list`), is kept, so a JSON list of records gives a YAML list of records.

## Inputs

Any JSON value.

## Outputs

The same value as YAML. A patch: what it gives is what it was given with `fmt=yaml` in place of `fmt=json`, and no `ext`. A JSON file gives YAML content, not a file; save it with a save cap to have a file.

## Notes

- For the reverse, use [Convert YAML to JSON](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;effect=patch;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;!ext";yaml-to-json).

args.name: input
args.arg_description: JSON to convert

caps.title: Convert YAML to JSON
caps.cap_description: Re-serialize any YAML value as JSON, keeping its shape
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Re-serializes any YAML value as JSON: a scalar, a list, a mapping or a list of mappings. The value's structure, and every marker that describes it (`list`, `record`, a named record), is kept, so a YAML list of records gives a JSON list of records.

## Inputs

Any YAML value.

## Outputs

The same value as JSON. A patch: what it gives is what it was given with `fmt=json` in place of `fmt=yaml`, and no `ext`. A YAML file gives JSON content, not a file; save it with a save cap to have a file.

## Notes

- For the reverse, use [Convert JSON to YAML](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;effect=patch;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json";json-to-yaml;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml;!ext").

args.name: input

caps.title: Convert CSV to JSON Array of Objects
caps.cap_description: Convert CSV data to a JSON array of objects with keys from the header row
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a CSV file into a JSON array of objects. Each data row becomes one JSON object; the CSV header row supplies the object keys. Use this when a downstream cap expects JSON but the data source is CSV.

## Inputs

A CSV file with a header row and one or more data rows.

## Outputs

A JSON array of objects, one per CSV row.

## Notes

- Column names from the header row become JSON keys. Sanitize column names upstream if they contain characters that are problematic as JSON keys.
- For YAML output, use [Convert CSV to YAML List of Mappings](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml;list;record").
- For the reverse, use [Convert JSON Array of Objects to CSV](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record").

Converts a CSV file into a YAML sequence of mappings. Each data row becomes one YAML mapping; the CSV header row supplies the keys. Use this when a downstream cap or tool expects YAML but the data source is CSV.

A CSV file with a header row and one or more data rows.

## Outputs

A YAML sequence of mappings, one per CSV row.

## Notes

- For JSON output instead, use [Convert CSV to JSON Array of Objects](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record").
- For the reverse, use [Convert YAML List of Mappings to CSV](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record").

Converts CSV data into a flat list of text values. Use this when you need the raw cell values from a CSV as individual text items, discarding the row/column structure.

A CSV file.

A list of UTF-8 text values (cells flattened from the CSV).

## Notes

- Row and column structure is lost; the output is a flat sequence of cell values.
- If you need to preserve row structure, use [Convert CSV to JSON Array of Objects](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record") instead.

A list of text values (one per array element).

caps.title: Convert JSON Array of Objects to CSV
caps.cap_description: Convert a JSON array of objects to CSV with headers derived from object keys
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Converts a JSON array of objects into a CSV file. Object keys become column headers; each array element becomes one row. Use this when downstream processing or export requires CSV format.

## Inputs

A JSON array where each element is an object.

## Outputs

A CSV file with a header row derived from the union of all object keys.

## Notes

- Objects with missing keys produce empty cells in those columns.
- Column order follows the key order of the first object (or union order if keys differ across objects).
- For the reverse, use [Convert CSV to JSON Array of Objects](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record").

Converts a YAML sequence into a flat list of text values. Use this when a downstream cap requires a plain text list but the upstream produces a YAML sequence.

A YAML sequence of scalar values.

## Outputs

A list of UTF-8 text values.

## Notes

- Non-string elements are converted to their string representations.
- For the reverse, use [Convert Text List to YAML Sequence](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;list";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml;list").

Converts a YAML sequence of mappings into a CSV file. Each mapping becomes one row; mapping keys become column headers. Use this when downstream processing requires tabular CSV but the data is in YAML format.

## Inputs

A YAML sequence where each element is a mapping.

## Outputs

A CSV file with headers derived from the mapping keys.

## Notes

- Mappings with missing keys produce empty cells.
- For JSON array output, use [Convert YAML to JSON](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;effect=patch;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;!ext";yaml-to-json), which keeps the list of mappings a list of records.
- For the reverse, use [Convert CSV to YAML List of Mappings](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-format;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record";out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=yaml;list;record").

Converts a flat list of text values into CSV format. Use this when downstream processing expects CSV but the upstream produces a plain text list.

## Notes

- If the list items are themselves comma-separated records, the output will be multi-column CSV. Otherwise each item maps to a single cell.

Decodes a GIF (first frame for animated GIFs) and writes it as a JPEG.

A JPEG file at quality 85.

caps.cap_description: Re-encode a GIF image as a PNG
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes a GIF (first frame for animated GIFs) and writes it as a PNG. Useful when downstream caps require PNG input.

## Inputs

A GIF file. For animated GIFs, the first frame is used.

## Outputs

A PNG file containing the (first) frame.

## Notes

- Animated GIF inputs convert their FIRST frame only (a warning is logged when frames are dropped). Full animation extraction is a different capability.

Animated GIFs collapse to their first frame. Transparency is preserved.

caps.title: Convert JPEG to PNG
caps.cap_description: Re-encode a JPEG image as a PNG
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes a JPEG image and re-encodes it as a lossless PNG. Use this when downstream cartridges only accept PNG (for example, [Describe Image (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:describe-image;candle;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text")), or when archiving JPEGs without further compression loss.

## Inputs

A JPEG file. The decoder accepts standard JFIF and Exif-tagged JPEGs.

## Outputs

A PNG file with the same pixel content.

## Notes

- EXIF orientation from the source is applied to the pixels, so the output displays upright even though the target format carries no orientation metadata.

The conversion is decode-then-encode. JPEG quantization artifacts are preserved exactly as a PNG cannot reverse them. PNG is larger on disk than the source JPEG for typical photographic content.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the JPEG file to convert

caps.title: Convert JPEG to WebP
caps.cap_description: Re-encode a JPEG image as a lossless WebP
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes a JPEG and writes it as a lossless WebP. Useful for archiving JPEGs without introducing further generation loss while reducing file size relative to PNG.

## Inputs

A JPEG file.

## Outputs

A lossless WebP file with the same pixel content.

## Notes

- EXIF orientation from the source is applied to the pixels, so the output displays upright even though the target format carries no orientation metadata.

The original JPEG quantization is preserved exactly; the WebP is lossless.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the JPEG file to convert

caps.title: Convert PNG to JPEG
caps.cap_description: Re-encode a PNG image as a JPEG
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes a PNG and re-encodes it as a JPEG. Use when a smaller file is preferred and the loss of transparency and the introduction of compression artifacts are acceptable.

## Inputs

A PNG file. RGBA inputs have the alpha channel composited against white.

## Outputs

A JPEG file at quality 85 (default, adjustable via --quality). EXIF orientation from the source is applied to the pixels, so the output displays upright.

## Notes

JPEG does not support transparency. Alpha is composited on a white background. Quality is fixed at 85; if you need different quality, request a feature.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the PNG file to convert

args.name: quality
args.arg_description: JPEG encode quality, 1-100

args.name: background
args.arg_description: Matte color (hex #RRGGBB) that transparency composites onto — JPEG has no alpha channel

caps.title: Convert PNG to WebP
caps.cap_description: Re-encode a PNG image as a lossless WebP
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes a PNG and writes it as a lossless WebP. Lossless WebP is typically smaller than PNG for the same pixel content.

## Inputs

A PNG file (with or without alpha).

## Outputs

A lossless WebP file with the same pixel content.

## Notes

This produces lossless WebP only. Lossy WebP encoding is not exposed.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the PNG file to convert

caps.title: Convert TIFF to JPEG

## Purpose

Decodes a TIFF (the first image in a multi-image TIFF) and writes it as a JPEG.

## Inputs

A TIFF file (uncompressed, LZW, PackBits or Deflate). Multi-page TIFFs use the first page.

## Outputs

A JPEG file at quality 85.

args.name: quality
args.arg_description: JPEG encode quality, 1-100

args.name: background
args.arg_description: Matte color (hex #RRGGBB) that transparency composites onto — JPEG has no alpha channel

caps.title: Convert TIFF to PNG
caps.cap_description: Re-encode a TIFF image as a PNG
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Decodes a TIFF (the first image in a multi-image TIFF) and writes it as a PNG. Useful when downstream caps require PNG input.

## Inputs

A TIFF file. For multi-page TIFFs, only the first page is used.

## Outputs

A PNG file with the same pixel content.

## Notes

- EXIF orientation from the source is applied to the pixels, so the output displays upright even though the target format carries no orientation metadata.

- Multi-page TIFF inputs convert their FIRST page only (a warning is logged when pages are dropped).

Uncompressed, LZW, PackBits and Deflate-compressed TIFFs are supported. JPEG-in-TIFF and CCITT fax compressions are not supported and will fail hard.

caps.title: Convert Image Format
caps.cap_description: Re-encode an image from one file format to another. Abstract: the concrete per-format cap is selected from the input file's type and the requested target.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

The generic form of the per-format image converters (e.g. [Convert JPEG to PNG](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-image;in="media:ext=jpeg;image";out="media:ext=png;image")). It is **abstract**: it names the operation (`convert-image`) and says both sides are an [image](https://capdag.com/browse/media:image), without pinning either format.

Running `convert-image <file> --to <format>` detects the input's media type, then narrows to the concrete converter for that source/target pair. Because an image can usually convert to more than one target, a target is required when the input alone is ambiguous — pass `--to png` (or `--to webp`, etc.). A file that is not an image is refused as such, and so is a target that is not an image format. It is never backed by a cartridge directly and never appears as a runnable edge in the cap graph; it is a dispatch umbrella and an alias target only.

## Inputs

Any image whose format a concrete `convert-image` cap implements.

## Outputs

The same image re-encoded in the requested target format.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the image file to convert

outputs.output_description: The re-encoded image in the requested target format.

Gives the Pearson correlation of two series at their shared instants.

caps.title: Decimate Sequence
caps.cap_description: Keep one item out of every N from an input sequence (drop the rest)
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Reduces the length of a sequence by keeping items at positions `0, N, 2N, ...` and dropping the rest. Useful for sub-sampling a long sequence — e.g. taking every 10th frame from `extract-frames`, every 5th record from a CSV, every Nth file from a folder.

## Inputs

- A sequence of any media type.
- An optional integer stride `N` (default: `1`, which is identity passthrough).

## Outputs

A sequence of the same media type as the input, containing approximately `ceil(input_count / N)` items. Per-item metadata on each kept item passes through unchanged.

## Notes

- The cap is generic over media (`in = media:`, `out = media:`); the planner routes it for any sequence input. The output's media URN matches the input's exactly — items themselves are passed through, not re-encoded.
- `--keep-every 1` (or omitting the argument) is exact passthrough.
- Negative, zero, or non-integer values fail loudly rather than silently being treated as 1; this is by design — a misspelled flag should surface, not be papered over.
- An empty input sequence is treated as a real input error (not a "successfully decimated zero items" success), since silently emitting an empty sequence would let downstream caps run on nothing without anyone noticing.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Sequence of items to decimate

args.name: keep-every
args.arg_description: Stride N: keep one item out of every N. Positive integer. Omit for passthrough.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Decimated sequence (same media type as input)

caps.title: Describe Image (GGUF) (GGUF (llama.cpp), ML Model, Vision)
caps.cap_description: Generate detailed image descriptions using GGUF multimodal models (moondream, Qwen3-VL, LLaVA, Gemma) with llama.cpp backend
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Generates detailed, instruction-following natural-language descriptions of PNG images using GGUF multimodal (vision-language) models via llama.cpp. Default is moondream2 2025-04-14, the GGUF vision model in the offline travel kit; also runs Qwen3-VL, SmolVLM2, LLaVA, Gemma, and any other GGUF VLM that ships a text+mmproj pair. The prompt can ask specific questions about image content.

## Inputs

- A GGUF vision model spec (HuggingFace repo or local path). Defaults to `ggml-org/moondream2-20250414-GGUF`.
- A PNG image file.
- A text prompt (default: "Describe this image in detail."). Customize to ask specific questions.
- Max tokens (default 256) and temperature (default 0.6).

## Outputs

A text description of the image as a plain string.

## Notes

- Vision-language models follow instructions in the prompt, making them more flexible than BLIP-style captioning models.
- Lower temperature (0.3-0.5) produces more factual, less creative descriptions.
- For Apple Silicon, prefer [Describe Image (MLX)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:describe-image;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;mlx;out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text";vision) for better performance.
- Input must be PNG. An image in another format is converted first with [Convert Image Format](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-image;in=media:image;out=media:image); a machine planned from a JPEG or WebP source takes that step by itself.

args.arg_description: System prompt that frames the model's behaviour for the request. Applied via the model's chat template when the downloaded VLM carries one (chat-template-jinja or chat-template-short); ignored for bare-prompt vision models such as GLM-OCR. Default is a generic helpful-assistant frame; concrete per-image instructions belong in the prompt slot.
args.default_value: You are a helpful assistant. Respond to the user's input with a useful, accurate, and concise reply. If the input is a document or excerpt, treat it as the subject of the user's request and respond about it.

args.name: temperature

caps.title: Describe Image (MLX) (ML Model, MLX (Apple Silicon), Vision)
caps.cap_description: Generate detailed image descriptions using MLX-based vision-language models on Apple Silicon
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Generates detailed, instruction-following natural-language descriptions of images using MLX-optimized vision-language models on Apple Silicon. Supports local file paths and HTTP(S) URLs as input. Delivers fast, energy-efficient vision inference on Mac M-series hardware.

## Inputs

- A model spec (MLX HuggingFace repo or local path). Defaults to `Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct-4bit`.
- A PNG image file (local path or HTTP(S) URL).
- A text prompt (default: "Describe this image in detail."). Customize to ask specific questions.
- Max tokens (default 256).

## Outputs

A text description of the image as a plain string.

## Notes

- Requires Apple Silicon (M1 or later).
- Input must be PNG. An image in another format is converted first with [Convert Image Format](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-image;in=media:image;out=media:image); a machine planned from a JPEG or WebP source takes that step by itself.
- Qwen3-VL and similar vision-language models can answer detailed questions, read text in images (OCR), identify objects, and describe scenes.
- This cap accepts HTTP(S) URLs directly in the file path argument, unlike the GGUF and Candle variants which require local paths.
- For cross-platform pipelines, use [Describe Image (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:describe-image;gguf;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text";vision).
