caps.title: Disbind PDF Into Per-Page PDFs
caps.cap_description: Split a PDF into a sequence of one-page PDFs
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Splits a PDF into a sequence of one-page PDFs — one item per page. Distinct from [Disbind PDF Into Page Text](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:disbind;in="media:document;ext=pdf";out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text") in that the output items are *PDF documents*, not page text. Use this when downstream caps want to operate on individual pages while keeping the PDF structure intact (e.g. per-page rendering with different parameters, per-page redaction, per-page binding back into a different order).

## Inputs

- A PDF file (path or stdin).
- An optional index range (default: `1-`, every page). Format: `1` (single page), `1-5` (pages 1-5), `3-` (page 3 to end).

## Outputs

A sequence of `media:document;ext=pdf` items, one valid one-page PDF per emitted page.

## Notes

- Index ranges support comma lists ('1,3,5-7'); ranges past the end clamp to the document. Encrypted PDFs need `--password`.

- Each emitted item is a complete standalone PDF with the page tree, resources, and metadata pdfium produces from the source page; downstream caps that load PDFs work on the items unchanged.
- An index range that matches no pages is a hard error — silently emitting an empty sequence would let downstream pipelines run on nothing without surfacing the empty-range mistake.
- For text-only extraction, use [Disbind PDF Into Page Text](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:disbind;in="media:document;ext=pdf";out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text").
- For the inverse (concatenating per-page PDFs back into one), use [Bind PDFs](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:bind;in="media:document;ext=pdf";out="media:document;ext=pdf").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the PDF file to process

args.name: index-range
args.arg_description: Pages to select (1-based). Grammar: '2', '1-5', '3-', '1,3,5-7'. Ranges past the end clamp to the document.

args.name: password
args.arg_description: Password for encrypted PDFs. Without it, an encrypted PDF fails with an error naming this flag; a wrong password fails saying so.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Per-page PDFs, one item per page

caps.title: Disbind PDF Into Pages
caps.cap_description: Extract plain text content from each PDF page
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Splits a PDF into its individual pages and extracts the plain text content from each page. The output is a sequence of text items, one per page. Use this as the first step in any PDF processing pipeline — text extraction, summarization, search indexing, or embedding.

## Inputs

- A PDF file (path or stdin).
- An optional index range (default: `1-`, meaning all pages). Format: `1` (single page), `1-5` (pages 1 to 5), `3-` (page 3 to end).

## Outputs

A sequence of plain text values, one item per extracted page.

## Notes

- A page whose text extraction fails emits an empty-text item with a warning (same shape as a scanned page) — one bad page never aborts the rest of the document. Encrypted PDFs need `--password`.

- Text extraction works on digitally-created PDFs. Scanned PDFs (image-only) will produce empty or near-empty pages. Run an OCR step first for scanned documents.
- For visual rendering of pages as images (e.g. to feed into vision models), use [Render PDF Page Images](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:render-page-image;in="media:document;ext=pdf";out="media:ext=png;image").
- Page numbers in the index range are 1-based.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the document file to process

args.name: index-range
args.arg_description: Pages to select (1-based). Grammar: '2', '1-5', '3-', '1,3,5-7'. Ranges past the end clamp to the document.

args.name: password
args.arg_description: Password for encrypted PDFs. Without it, an encrypted PDF fails with an error naming this flag; a wrong password fails saying so.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Plain text pages, one per page in the document; each page is persistable as a `.txt` file

caps.title: Disbind Document Into Pages
caps.cap_description: Extract plain text from each page of a document. Abstract: the concrete per-format cap is selected from the input file's type.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

The generic form of the page-text extractors (e.g. [Disbind PDF](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:disbind;in="media:document;ext=pdf";out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text")). It is **abstract**: it names an operation (`disbind`), says its input is a [document](https://capdag.com/browse/media:document) and its output page text, without pinning the document's format.

Running `disbind <file>` detects the input's media type and narrows to the concrete cap that handles it — `disbind <doc>.pdf` runs the PDF extractor. A file that is not a document is refused as such. It is never backed by a cartridge directly and never appears as a runnable edge in the cap graph; it is a dispatch umbrella and an alias target only.

## Inputs

Any document whose file type a concrete `disbind` cap implements. The output is always a sequence of plain-text pages regardless of the source format.

## Outputs

A sequence of plain text values, one item per page.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the document file to process

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Plain text pages, one per page in the document.

caps.title: Download Model
caps.cap_description: Download a model from repository to local cache.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Downloads a model from a remote repository (e.g. HuggingFace) to the local model cache. Subsequent inference caps will use the cached copy without network access.

## Inputs

A model spec string (e.g. `hf:org/model-name` or `hf:org/model-name?include=*.gguf`). Include/exclude filters in the spec control which files are downloaded.

## Outputs

A JSON record with the local cache path, downloaded file list, and download metadata.

## Notes

- Downloads are resumable at byte granularity: an interrupted direct download keeps its partial file and the next run continues from where it stopped with an HTTP Range request; mid-stream network failures retry with a resume automatically. When `verify_checksums` is on (the default), direct downloads are sha256-verified against the repository's LFS hash while streaming — a mismatch deletes the corrupt file and fails hard naming both hashes.
- The HuggingFace endpoint honors the ecosystem-standard `HF_ENDPOINT` environment variable (enterprise mirrors, air-gapped proxies).
- Use `include`/`exclude` filters in the model spec to download only the quantization variant you need rather than the full repository.
- Check progress of an ongoing download with [Model Status](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";model-status;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-status;record").
- After downloading, confirm the local path with [Get Model Path](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";model-path;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-path;record").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Model spec (e.g., hf:org/model-name)

args.name: expected-pattern
args.arg_description: Consumer cap's expected model-spec pattern URN. The pattern's dims (backend, repo-format, family, model-task, chat-template, tokenizer-shape, quantisation) are hard requirements the downloaded model MUST satisfy. The user's `?include=`/`?exclude=` on the model_spec arg is a soft hint within this pattern's space; if it conflicts with the pattern the user filter is dropped (with a warn log) and the cap floor wins. Pattern not satisfiable by the repo ⇒ hard error before any bytes are fetched. Wired as a CLI flag because bifaci permits only one stdin-sourced arg per cap and that slot belongs to the model-spec.

args.name: hf-token
args.arg_description: HuggingFace bearer token. Required when downloading a gated repository (license-protected models). Without it, gated downloads fail with a clear authentication error rather than silently falling back to anonymous access.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Download result with model path and metadata

caps.title: Edit (Instruction-Driven Transform)
caps.cap_description: Transform JSON records by plain-language instruction via a generated, logged, deterministic program
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

"Describe the transformation like you would to a chatbot, get a Unix tool": `edit --instruction "keep only active users, lowercase their emails, sort by name"` over a JSON array of records. The model translates the instruction into a program in a closed operation language (select/drop/rename/set/filter/map/sort/limit/reverse), token-level constrained to the program schema — an ill-formed program is impossible by construction. The program is logged in full BEFORE it runs, then executes deterministically. The model never touches the data: it sees only the instruction and a bounded structural sample (field names and types from the first records).

Fuzzy in, auditable and replayable out — the logged program re-run on tomorrow's file produces tomorrow's answer by the same rules.

Part of the semantic-primitive cap family (docs/semantic-primitives.md, Group 2).

## Inputs

- A JSON array of objects (stdin or first positional argument).
- `--instruction`: the transformation in plain language (required).

## Outputs

The transformed JSON array of records.

## Notes

- Program generation is deterministic (law P4): the same instruction and record structure produce the same program.
- Execution errors are hard and name the record index, field, and rule (e.g. lowercasing a number) — never silent skips.
- Requires the GGUF inference cartridge (constrained generation) to be installed.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: The JSON array of records to transform

args.name: instruction
args.arg_description: The transformation, described in plain language

args.name: model-spec
args.arg_description: Model spec used to generate the transform program

caps.title: Get Embeddings Dimensions (MLX) (ML Model, MLX (Apple Silicon))
caps.cap_description: Query the dimensionality of embeddings for a given MLX model
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Reports the vector size that an MLX embedding model produces. Requires Apple Silicon. Use this before creating a vector index so you know how many dimensions to allocate.

## Inputs

- A model spec pointing to an MLX embedding model directory or HuggingFace repo. Defaults to `mlx-community/all-MiniLM-L6-v2-4bit`, the MLX embeddings model in the offline travel kit.

## Outputs

A single integer: the number of dimensions in each embedding vector this model produces.

## Notes

- Reads model configuration only — no inference is run, so it is fast.
- MLX models are quantized for efficiency on Apple Silicon; verify that the quantization level is compatible with your accuracy requirements.
- See also: [Generate Vector Embeddings (MLX)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:generate-embeddings;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";ml-model;mlx;out="media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record")

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to MLX embedding model directory

caps.title: Encode Audio Frames as WAV
caps.cap_description: Assemble a PCM audio-frame sequence (live microphone capture or replay) into a single WAV file
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Folds a sequence of raw PCM audio frames — the CONTENT a resolved live
microphone feed delivers (13.2 §Reference Media) — into one WAV file. This
is the bridge between live audio capture and every WAV-consuming cap:
`microphone → encode-audio-frames-wav → transcribe` is the canonical live
transcription machine, and `microphone → encode-audio-frames-wav` alone is
a recorder.

## Inputs

A sequence of `media:audio;audio-frames;pcm` items: signed 16-bit little-endian
interleaved PCM buffers. The stream-level metadata MUST carry the capture
format actuals (`sample_rate`, `channels`) — a frame stream without them
cannot be encoded and fails loudly.

## Outputs

One WAV file (PCM s16le) containing every delivered frame, in capture
order.

## Notes

- This is a FOLD with deferred emission (15.2 §Live-Feed Machines): over a
  live feed the WAV materializes when the feed ends — a stop condition
  fires, or the run is stopped (close-tap-and-drain). A stopped recording
  is a valid, complete recording.
- Overrun gaps (12.5 §Overrun) are genuine discontinuities: the dropped
  frames are simply absent from the file. The gap accounting stays on the
  run's protocol counters — nothing is silently synthesized to paper over
  loss.
- An empty frame sequence is a real input error, not an empty WAV: a feed
  that delivered nothing means the capture never produced data, and
  downstream caps must not run on a silent zero-length file.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Sequence of raw PCM (s16le) audio frame buffers with sample_rate/channels stream metadata

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: A single WAV (PCM s16le) file assembled from the frame sequence

args.name: rate-in

caps.title: Extract Audio Track from MP4
caps.cap_description: Demux the audio track from an MP4 video and write it as an M4A file
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Extracts the AAC audio track from an MP4 container and writes it as an M4A file (the same AAC bitstream, re-containered without re-encoding). This is the canonical first step when you have a video and want to feed its audio into a transcription pipeline.

An MP4 file with an AAC audio track. Video tracks are ignored.

An M4A file containing the source's AAC audio track. No re-encoding occurs; the AAC bitstream is bit-exact.

If the MP4 has no AAC audio track, the cap fails hard. There is no audio re-encoding fallback.

caps.documentation:
## Purpose

It is **abstract**: it names the operation (`extract-audio-track`), says its input is a [video](https://capdag.com/browse/media:video) and its output [audio](https://capdag.com/browse/media:audio), without pinning the container or the audio format.

Running `extract-audio-track <file>` detects the input's media type and narrows to the concrete cap for that container — `extract-audio-track clip.mkv` runs the MKV extractor and writes Opus. Each container has one extractor, so the input alone decides the output format. A file that is not a video is refused as such. It is never backed by a cartridge directly and never appears as a runnable edge in the cap graph; it is a dispatch umbrella and an alias target only.

## Inputs

Any video whose container a concrete `extract-audio-track` cap implements.

## Outputs

The audio track, in the format the container's extractor writes: Opus from MKV and WebM, M4A from MP4 and MOV. No re-encoding occurs.

## Purpose

Decodes a Matroska MKV video and emits its frames as a sequence of PNG images. With no `--fps` argument every decoded frame is emitted; with `--fps N`, frames are decimated to approximately `N` per second by selecting the first decoded frame whose presentation timestamp passes each `1/N`-second boundary.

- An MKV file (path or stdin).
- An optional target frame rate (default: every frame).

A sequence of PNG images, one per emitted frame.

- Decoding happens in-process via embedded ffmpeg static archives — no system ffmpeg dependency, no shell-out.
- For audio extraction from the same file, use [Extract Audio Track from MKV](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:extract-audio-track;in="media:ext=mkv;video";out="media:audio;ext=opus").

caps.title: Look Up Cap Definition (Fabric)
caps.cap_description: Resolve a canonical cap URN to its full registry-published cap definition by fetching from the public fabric registry.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose
Resolves a canonical cap URN to the full flattened cap definition the registry
publisher produced for it. The result is the registry's authoritative shape —
including each argument's `default_value`, the output media URN, documentation,
and any metadata.

## Inputs
- A canonical cap URN string. The string is re-parsed through the cap URN parser
  on receipt; non-parseable values are rejected with a hard error.

## Outputs
A JSON record carrying the full flattened cap entry (see
`media:cap-definition;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record` for the schema).

## Notes
- Sandboxed cartridges call this cap as a peer to read registry data without
  needing direct internet access. The cartridge implementation lives in a
  non-sandboxed engine-bundled cartridge.
- Lookups are cached by canonical URN; cache misses fail hard rather than
  returning empty results, exposing missing-from-registry conditions instead
  of silently degrading.
- The cap URN is a tagged URN. Equality is double-sided `conforms_to`; never
  compare URN strings byte-for-byte. The cartridge canonicalises through the
  parser before hashing for cache keys.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Canonical cap URN to look up.

args.name: defver
args.arg_description: Per-definition version under the caller's manifest snapshot, 1 or greater. Absent ⇒ resolved under the fabric manifest the lookup cartridge is pinned to; a URN that manifest does not list is not found.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Full flattened cap definition as published in the registry.

caps.title: Generate Vector Embeddings (GGUF) (GGUF (llama.cpp), ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Generate vector embeddings from text using GGUF models with llama.cpp backend
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Encodes text into dense floating-point vectors using quantized GGUF embedding models via llama.cpp. Suitable for semantic search, clustering, and RAG. Long documents are automatically split into overlapping chunks.

## Inputs

- A GGUF model spec (HuggingFace repo or local path). Defaults to `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5-GGUF`, the GGUF embeddings model in the offline travel kit.
- A text file to embed.
- Chunk size in words (default 400), chunk overlap in words (default 50), and batch size in tokens (default 2048).

## Outputs

A JSON record containing an array of embedding objects. Each object includes the chunk text, its position, the L2-normalized embedding vector, and model metadata.

## Notes

- GGUF quantization makes models smaller and faster at a small accuracy trade-off. Q4 and Q8 quantizations are common choices.
- Vectors are L2-normalized. Use cosine similarity or dot product when comparing vectors from this cap.
- Batch size is a per-decode memory bound, never a correctness ceiling: a chunk whose tokenization exceeds the usable window (the smaller of the model's trained context and the batch size) is embedded window-by-window and the window embeddings are mean-pooled weighted by token count, then L2-normalized — the whole chunk always contributes.
- Use [Get Embeddings Dimensions (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:embeddings-dimensions;gguf;in="media:embeddings;enc=utf8;gguf;model-spec;tokenizer-embedded-gguf";ml-model;out="media:integer;model-dim;numeric") to check the vector size.
- For Apple Silicon, prefer [Generate Vector Embeddings (MLX)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:generate-embeddings;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";ml-model;mlx;out="media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record").

args.name: model-spec
args.arg_description: GGUF model specification (HuggingFace repo or local path)

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to text file to generate embeddings from

args.name: chunk-size
args.arg_description: Chunk size in words for splitting input text

args.name: chunk-overlap
args.arg_description: Chunk overlap in words when splitting input text

args.name: batch-size
args.arg_description: Per-decode token window bound (memory knob). Chunks tokenizing past the usable window are embedded window-by-window and mean-pooled — never rejected or truncated.

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON containing L2-normalized embeddings, chunk metadata and model information

caps.title: Generate Vector Embeddings (MLX) (MLX (Apple Silicon), ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Generate vector embeddings from text using MLX-based models on Apple Silicon
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Encodes text into dense floating-point vectors using MLX-optimized embedding models on Apple Silicon. Delivers fast, energy-efficient embedding on Mac M-series hardware. Long documents are automatically chunked.

## Inputs

- A model spec (HuggingFace repo or local path). Defaults to `mlx-community/all-MiniLM-L6-v2-4bit`, the MLX embeddings model in the offline travel kit.
- A text file to embed.
- Chunk size in words (default 400) and chunk overlap in words (default 50).

## Outputs

A JSON record containing an array of embedding objects with chunk text, position, embedding vector, and model metadata.

## Notes

- A chunk whose tokenization exceeds the model's positional capacity (512 tokens for MiniLM-class models) is embedded window-by-window and the window embeddings are mean-pooled weighted by token count, then L2-normalized — the whole chunk always contributes; nothing is rejected or silently truncated.

- Requires Apple Silicon (M1 or later). Not available on Intel Macs or non-Apple hardware.
- MLX uses the unified memory architecture; large models share CPU/GPU memory without copying.
- Use [Get Embeddings Dimensions (MLX)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:embeddings-dimensions;in="media:embeddings;enc=utf8;mlx;model-spec";ml-model;mlx;out="media:integer;model-dim;numeric") to check the vector size.
- For cross-platform pipelines, use [Generate Vector Embeddings (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:candle;generate-embeddings;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";ml-model;out="media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") or [Generate Vector Embeddings (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:generate-embeddings;gguf;in="media:enc=utf8;plain-text";ml-model;out="media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") instead.

args.name: model
args.arg_description: Path to MLX embedding model directory

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to text file to generate embeddings from

args.name: chunk-size
args.arg_description: Chunk size in words for splitting input text

args.name: chunk-overlap
args.arg_description: Chunk overlap in words when splitting input text

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON containing embeddings, chunk metadata and model information

caps.title: Generate Text with LLM (GGUF) (GGUF (llama.cpp), LLM, ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Generate text using GGUF models with llama.cpp backend
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Accepts a raw text prompt and generates a text continuation using a quantized GGUF model via llama.cpp. This is a simpler prompt-in / text-out interface. Offers more sampling controls than the Candle equivalent (top-k, min-p, repetition penalty, context length).

## Inputs

- A text prompt (plain text). Prompts of any size that fit the model's trained context work out of the box: the context window is auto-sized to prompt + max-tokens and the prompt is prefilled in batch-sized windows.
- A GGUF model spec (HuggingFace repo or local path). Defaults to `bartowski/Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct-GGUF` Q4_K_M, the GGUF LLM in the offline travel kit.
- Sampling parameters: max tokens (512), temperature (0.7), top-k (40), top-p (0.9), min-p (0.05), repetition penalty (1.1), seed (42), max context length (unset = auto), batch size (2048).

## Outputs

Generated text streamed as raw text chunks (not NDJSON).

## Notes

- For structured output, system prompts, or streaming JSON events, use [LLM Text Generation (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:llm-inference;gguf;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-generation-request;record";llm;ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream") instead.
- Context sizing: leaving `--max-context-length` UNSET auto-sizes the context to prompt + max-tokens, capped at the model's trained context — memory stays proportional to actual need. A value is an explicit resource bound (also capped at the trained context); if the prompt leaves no generation room inside it, the cap fails hard with the exact token counts. Input is never silently truncated.
- Batch size is tokens-per-decode-call during prompt prefill — a throughput/memory knob. It never limits prompt length.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Input text prompt for generation

args.name: system-prompt
args.arg_description: System prompt that frames the model's behaviour for the request. Applied via the model's chat template when the downloaded model carries one (chat-template-jinja or chat-template-short); ignored for base/completion models. Default is a generic helpful-assistant frame that works for arbitrary user input — task-specific prompts (summarise, translate, explain) belong in the user-message slot.
args.default_value: You are a helpful assistant. Respond to the user's input with a useful, accurate, and concise reply. If the input is a document or excerpt, treat it as the subject of the user's request and respond about it.

args.name: model-spec
args.arg_description: GGUF model specification (HuggingFace repo or local path)

args.name: hf-token
args.arg_description: HuggingFace bearer token. Required when targeting a gated repository. Without it, gated downloads fail with a clear authentication error.

args.name: max-tokens
args.arg_description: Maximum number of tokens to generate

args.name: temperature
args.arg_description: Sampling temperature (0.0-2.0)

args.name: top-k
args.arg_description: Top-k sampling parameter

args.name: top-p
args.arg_description: Top-p (nucleus) sampling parameter

args.name: min-p
args.arg_description: Min-p sampling parameter

args.name: seed
args.arg_description: Random seed for reproducibility

args.name: max-context-length
args.arg_description: Maximum context length. Leave unset to auto-size to prompt + max-tokens, capped at the model's trained context. A value is an explicit resource bound (also capped at the trained context); a prompt that leaves no generation room inside it fails hard with exact token counts — input is never silently truncated.

args.name: batch-size
args.arg_description: Tokens per decode call during prompt prefill — a throughput/memory knob. Never limits prompt length.

args.name: repetition-penalty
args.arg_description: Repetition penalty

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Generated text streamed as raw text chunks

caps.title: LLM Text Generation (GGUF) (GGUF (llama.cpp), LLM, ML Model)
caps.cap_description: Generate text using GGUF models with llama.cpp backend. Output is NDJSON streaming tokens.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Runs autoregressive text generation using quantized GGUF models via llama.cpp. Accepts a fully-structured generation request and streams output as NDJSON tokens. This is the primary low-level inference cap for GGUF-based pipelines.

## Inputs

A single JSON generation request record containing: the prompt, model spec (HuggingFace GGUF repo or local path), sampling parameters (temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p, repeat penalty, max tokens, seed, context length), and an optional system prompt. Context length 0 (or omitted) auto-sizes to prompt + max-tokens, capped at the model's trained context; the prompt prefills in batch-sized windows, so batch size never limits prompt length and input is never silently truncated.

Optional HuggingFace bearer token (`hf_token`) for gated repositories.

## Outputs

An NDJSON stream. Each line is a JSON object carrying token text, status events (`started`, `complete`), and a final summary with token counts and timing.

## Notes

- Every execution is streaming — there is no non-streaming mode.
- GGUF quantization reduces memory requirements significantly. Q8_0 preserves most accuracy; Q4_K_M is a good balance of size and quality.
- For constrained output (JSON schema, regex), use [Constrained LLM Generation (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:llm-inference-constrained;constrained;gguf;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-generation-request;record";llm;ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream").
- For Apple Silicon, prefer [LLM Text Generation (MLX)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:llm-inference;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-generation-request;record";llm;ml-model;mlx;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream").

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Extracts the full token vocabulary from a GGUF model. The vocabulary is required by LLGuidance and other constrained decoding backends before they can compile JSON schemas, regexes, or grammars into token-level masks.

- The vocab array indices correspond to token IDs used internally by the model's tokenizer.
- See also: [Constrained LLM Generation (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:llm-inference-constrained;constrained;gguf;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-generation-request;record";llm;ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream") which depends on this vocabulary.

caps.title: OCR (GGUF) (GGUF (llama.cpp), ML Model, OCR)
caps.cap_description: Digitize verbatim text from an image with a GGUF OCR vision model (default GLM-OCR)
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Reads an image and returns the literal text written inside it. Uses a dedicated GGUF
OCR vision-language model via llama.cpp's multimodal (mtmd) API. The default model is
[GLM-OCR](https://huggingface.co/ggml-org/GLM-OCR-GGUF) — a 0.9B-parameter OCR
specialist that reaches state-of-the-art OmniDocBench scores while remaining small
enough to run quickly on CPU or Metal.

This cap is for *transcription* of text that appears in an image, not for *describing*
what the image depicts. For descriptions, use [Describe Image (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:describe-image;gguf;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text";vision).

## Inputs

- A GGUF OCR model spec (HuggingFace repo or local path). Defaults to `hf:ggml-org/GLM-OCR-GGUF`.
- A PNG image file.
- A text prompt that nudges the model's output format. Defaults to `"OCR"`. OCR-specialised
  GGUF models recognise short directive prompts — try `"OCR markdown"` to preserve layout
  as Markdown, or `"OCR HTML table"` for tabular content.
- Max tokens (default 1024 — OCR output is often longer than a caption) and temperature
  (default 0.0 — OCR is a deterministic transcription task; randomness only adds errors).

## Outputs

The recognised text as plain UTF-8. When prompted with `"OCR markdown"` the same channel
carries Markdown-formatted text — still UTF-8 text and still flows into any text consumer.

## Notes

- Best results on screenshots, scanned pages, and photographs of printed text. Handwriting
  is supported but harder; expect more errors on cursive or low-contrast samples.
- OCR models perform poorly when asked to *describe* an image — they are trained for
  transcription. Pick the right cap for the job.
- Lower temperature (0.0–0.2) yields cleaner transcriptions. Higher values increase
  hallucinated characters and should be avoided for OCR.
- The model file plus its mmproj projector is ~1 GB at Q8_0 quantisation; first run
  triggers a one-time download via the model cartridge.
- Input must be PNG. An image in another format is converted first with [Convert Image Format](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:convert-image;in=media:image;out=media:image); a machine planned from a JPEG or WebP source takes that step by itself.

args.name: model-spec
args.arg_description: GGUF OCR model specification (HuggingFace repo or local path)

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the image file to transcribe

args.name: prompt
args.arg_description: Directive prompt for the OCR model (e.g. "OCR", "OCR markdown", "OCR HTML table")

args.name: system-prompt
args.arg_description: System prompt that frames the OCR model's behaviour. Applied via the model's chat template when the downloaded model carries one (chat-template-jinja or chat-template-short); ignored for bare-prompt OCR specialists such as GLM-OCR. Default is a generic helpful-assistant frame; the per-image directive ("OCR markdown", "transcribe receipts") belongs in the prompt slot.

args.name: model-loading
args.arg_description: How the model's files are brought into memory: `map` memory-maps them, `read` reads them whole, `auto` maps from a local disk and reads from a network filesystem.

caps.cap_description: Read a PDF filing into its passages, page by page, its pages read by pdfcartridge and an OCR cap
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Reads a PDF into passages under their headings, page by page. The pages are read by other cartridges, asked as peers: pdfcartridge's disbind-pdf for each page's text, and for a page with none (a picture of text) render-page-image-pdf for its picture and the OCR cap for the text in it.

## Inputs

- A PDF document.

## Outputs

The filing's content; a page read from its picture says so where it is.

## Notes

A PDF's tables are not recovered as tables: that takes where each word stands, which the page text does not carry. A PDF with no text even in its pictures is refused as an input failure. When pdfcartridge or the OCR cap cannot be asked, the failure is the environment's.

caps.title: Render PDF Page Images
caps.cap_description: Render PNG page images for one or more PDF pages
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Renders one or more pages of a PDF as PNG images. Each page becomes a separate PNG output. Use this to feed PDF content into vision models, generate thumbnails, or produce visual previews.

## Inputs

- A PDF file (path or stdin).
- Page image width in pixels (default 800).
- Page image height in pixels (default 1200).
- An optional index range (default: `1-`, all pages). Format: `1` (single page), `1-5` (pages 1-5), `3-` (page 3 to end). Ranges are 1-based.

## Outputs

A sequence of PNG images, one per rendered page.

## Notes

- Index ranges support comma lists ('1,3,5-7'); ranges past the end clamp to the document. Encrypted PDFs need `--password` (the error names the flag when it is missing or wrong).

- Higher resolution (larger width/height) produces more readable images at the cost of larger file sizes.
- Feed the PNG output into [Describe Image (MLX)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:describe-image;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;mlx;out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text";vision) or [Generate Image Embeddings (Candle)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:generate-image-embeddings;candle;in="media:ext=png;image";ml-model;out="media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") for vision-based PDF analysis.
- For plain text extraction, use [Disbind PDF Into Pages](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:disbind;in="media:document;ext=pdf";out="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text") instead.

caps.title: Repair CSV
caps.cap_description: Repair broken CSV (BOM, short rows) with every fix logged; unguessable damage stays a hard error
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Explicit forgiveness for CSV (docs/semantic-primitives.md, law P9): strips a UTF-8 byte-order mark and pads rows SHORTER than the header out to the header width, logging every fix with its position. Quoting is normalized as a side effect of re-serialization through a strict writer.

## Inputs

The broken CSV text (stdin or first positional argument).

## Outputs

CSV with uniform row width and normalized quoting.

## Notes

- Rows with MORE fields than the header are a hard error naming the row: extra fields are data (usually an unquoted delimiter in the source), and merging or dropping them would be a guess.
- Deterministic: no model is involved.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: The broken CSV text to repair

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Repaired CSV with uniform row width and normalized quoting

caps.title: Repair JSON
caps.cap_description: Repair broken JSON with every fix logged — explicit forgiveness so strict caps can stay strict
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

The explicit-forgiveness step of the semantic-primitive family (docs/semantic-primitives.md, law P9): the strict data caps stay strict, and when real-world input is broken — single quotes, unquoted keys, trailing or missing commas, Python literals (`True`/`None`), `NaN`/`Infinity`, comments, truncated documents — `repair` fixes it VISIBLY. Every fix is logged with its byte position and a one-sentence description, so a pipeline that needs leniency writes `repair | convert-…` and the leniency is on the record.

## Inputs

The broken JSON text (stdin or first positional argument).

## Outputs

Strictly valid JSON, of whatever shape the input was: a value, a list, a record or a list of records. The output says it may be a list and may be a record (`?list;?record`), since which it is depends on the input.

## Notes

- Valid JSON round-trips untouched (zero repairs logged) — repair is idempotent on clean input.
- Repairs happen only where the intended structure is unambiguous. Anything that would require guessing at DATA — trailing content after a complete document, unknown bare words — is a hard error naming the byte position. A wrong guess silently propagated is worse than a loud stop.
- Deterministic: no model is involved; the same input always repairs the same way.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: The broken JSON text to repair

caps.title: Save as CSV
caps.cap_description: Save a CSV list of records as a `.csv` file that reads back as what it is. Bytes pass through unchanged.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Terminal cap that writes a CSV list of records to disk as a `.csv` file. Content is no file
type: a cap that gives a CSV list of records gives it without a file extension, and this cap is
how that content becomes a file a plan can end on.

The output is exactly the type detection reads back from the file it writes, so
a value saved here and opened again is what it was saved as.

## Inputs

- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=csv;list;record;!ext` — a CSV list of records that is not yet a file.

## Outputs

- `media:enc=utf8;ext=csv;fmt=csv;list;record` — the same bytes, as a `.csv` file.

## Notes

- No conversion and no re-encoding: the bytes pass through unchanged.
- The cap checks the content first: content that would read back from a `.csv`
  file as another type is refused, naming what it reads back as.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: a CSV list of records to save as a `.csv` file

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: The same bytes, as a `.csv` file

  file as a type outside its output is refused, naming what it reads back as.

caps.title: Render Log Page Image
caps.cap_description: Render a page-like PNG image preview of the log document
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Renders a log file as a page-like PNG image. Useful for generating visual snapshots of log output for display in dashboards, reports, or image-aware pipeline steps.

## Inputs

- A log file (path or stdin, media type `media:enc=utf8;ext=log;plain-text`).
- Page width in pixels (default 800).
- Page height in pixels (default 1200).

## Outputs

A sequence of PNG images, one per page.

## Notes

- For plain text files that are not log files, use [Render Text Page Image](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:render-page-image;in="media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text";out="media:ext=png;image").
- Long documents paginate: the text is wrapped to the page width by measured glyph advance (long lines wrap, they are never clipped) and split into as many pages as needed. Nothing is truncated.
- Invalid UTF-8 bytes render as the replacement character (U+FFFD) — the page shows exactly what was recoverable instead of the file being rejected.
- Tail the log upstream (or use --index-range) if you only need recent entries.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Path to the log file to process

args.name: width
args.arg_description: Width of the page image in pixels

args.name: height
args.arg_description: Height of the page image in pixels

args.name: index-range
args.arg_description: Pages to render (1-based). Grammar: '2', '1-5', '3-', '1,3,5-7'. Ranges past the end clamp to the document.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: PNG page images, one per rendered page

caps.title: Save as Plain Text
caps.cap_description: Persist a finalised plain-text value as a `.txt` file. Bytes pass through unchanged.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Terminal cap for finalised plain text. The input must already carry the
`plain-text` marker — caps that produce user-facing prose (LLM text-generation,
OCR's digitized text, summarisation) declare `media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text` as
their `out`, and this cap is the registered terminal that writes such values to
disk as `.txt`.

The narrow `in` is intentional. An earlier version accepted `media:enc=utf8`,
which polluted the planner's recommended-paths surface — every text-producing
cap (PDF page extractor, JSON-as-text adapter, prompt loader) became a feeder
for `.txt` persistence even when the result wasn't meaningful prose. The
`plain-text` marker is an explicit "yes, this is finished text suitable for a
`.txt` file" opt-in.

## Inputs

- `media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text` — finalised plain-text bytes.

## Outputs

The same bytes, same URN. The cap is a relabel-and-persist; the writer derives
the `.txt` extension from the URN's existing `file-type=txt` narrowing.

## Notes

- No conversion. No re-encoding. No content inspection. Byte-for-byte passthrough.
- To save text from a producer that emits `media:enc=utf8` (not `plain-text`),
  the producer must be updated to declare the `plain-text` opt-in, OR a
  format-specific intermediate cap must be inserted to relabel the value.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: The finalised plain-text value to persist as a `.txt` file

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: The same bytes, persisted as a `.txt` file

caps.title: Try Forecasting Ways
caps.cap_description: Try ways of forecasting a change in a series on its history: choose on each stretch, score on the next
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Hindcasts a statement about a series (will it end, or ever be, so many percent above or below where it stands, so many days ahead): through history, at moments `every-days` apart, each way of forecasting says a probability from what was known then; the moments are cut into stretches, the way that did best before each stretch is chosen and scored on it.

## Inputs

- A time series.
- `comparison`, `change-pct`, `window`: the statement.
- `days`, `every-days`, `stretches`: the trial.

## Outputs

A forecast trial.

## Notes

A rule that only looked good on the history it was chosen on shows here as a chosen score no better than saying 50% every time.

args.name: series
args.arg_description: The series

args.name: comparison
args.arg_description: How the change is compared: above, below, at_least or at_most

args.name: change-pct
args.arg_description: The change asked about, in percent

args.name: window
args.arg_description: When the statement must hold: at_deadline or any_time

args.name: days
args.arg_description: How far ahead each forecast looks, in days

args.name: every-days
args.arg_description: Days between moments

args.name: stretches
args.arg_description: How many test stretches

caps.cap_description: Resample a series to a calendar period: one value per period, its observations combined
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Turns a series of any frequency into one of a calendar period (daily to annual): each period with observations gets one value, combined by the aggregate chosen and stamped at the period's last observation.

## Inputs

- A time series.
- `every`: the period.
- `aggregate`: last, mean or sum.

## Outputs

A time series with one value per period that has observations.

## Notes

Periods with no observation are left out, not filled.

args.name: every
args.arg_description: The period: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or annual

args.name: aggregate
args.arg_description: How a period's observations become its value: last, mean or sum

caps.title: Rolling Statistic
caps.cap_description: Take a statistic of a series over a moving window: its mean, standard deviation, z-score, or volatility scaled to a year
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Turns a series into a rolling statistic: at each instant, the mean, standard deviation, z-score or volatility of the `window` observations ending there.

## Inputs

- A time series.
- `window`: how many observations.
- `statistic`: mean, sd, zscore or vol.
- `periods-per-year`: how many observations a year holds. Given with `vol`, and only with it.

## Outputs

The rolling statistic, starting where the first full window ends.

## Notes

`vol` is the window's sample standard deviation times the square root of `periods-per-year`, of the series as given and in its units: for a series of changes (daily returns, say) it is their realised volatility for a year. It is not worked out from prices; for a price path, take its changes first. `vol` without `periods-per-year` is refused, naming it, and `periods-per-year` with another statistic is refused.

A z-score over a window that does not move is left out for that instant and counted.

args.name: series
args.arg_description: The series

args.name: window
args.arg_description: How many observations each value is taken over

args.name: statistic
args.arg_description: Which statistic: mean, sd, zscore or vol

args.name: periods-per-year
args.arg_description: How many observations a year holds; given with vol, which it scales to a year

## Inputs

- `window`.
- `periods-per-year`.

## Outputs

A time series of volatility, as a fraction a year.

## Notes

A path at zero or below is refused.

args.arg_description: The price path

args.name: window

args.name: periods-per-year
args.arg_description: How many observations a year holds

caps.title: Regress Series
caps.cap_description: Fit one series on one or more others by ordinary least squares, giving the fit and its residuals
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Measures how much a dependent series moves with one or more regressors, on the instants they all have: `y = alpha + betas · x`.

## Inputs

- `y`: the dependent time series (the main input).
- `x`: one or more regressor series, in order.

## Outputs

- The regression (main output).
- `residuals`: what the fit leaves at each instant, as a time series.

## Notes

Name the regressors in a machine, once each: `(y, x=a, x=b) -> regress-series -> (fit, residuals=res)`. Refused with too few shared instants to identify the coefficients, or regressors that do not move or move together.

args.name: y
args.arg_description: The dependent series

args.name: x
args.arg_description: The regressor series, in order

outputs.name: residuals
outputs.output_description: What the fit leaves unexplained at each instant

## Notes

caps.title: LLM Text Generation (MLX) (LLM, ML Model, MLX (Apple Silicon))
caps.cap_description: Generate text using MLX models on Apple Silicon. Output is NDJSON streaming tokens.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Runs autoregressive text generation using MLX-optimized models on Apple Silicon. Accepts a fully-structured generation request and streams output as NDJSON tokens. Designed for fast, energy-efficient inference on Mac M-series hardware.

## Inputs

A single JSON generation request record containing: the prompt, model spec (MLX HuggingFace repo or local path), sampling parameters (temperature, top-p, repeat penalty, max tokens, seed), and an optional system prompt.

## Outputs

An NDJSON stream. Each line is a JSON object carrying token text, status events (`started`, `complete`), and a final summary with token counts and timing.

## Notes

- Requires Apple Silicon (M1 or later).
- MLX uses unified memory — models share CPU/GPU memory without copying, giving practical access to large models on machines with ample RAM.
- Every execution is streaming.
- For cross-platform pipelines, use [LLM Text Generation (GGUF)](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:llm-inference;gguf;in="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-generation-request;record";llm;ml-model;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: The generation request containing prompt, model spec, and parameters

args.name: hf-token
args.arg_description: HuggingFace bearer token. Required when targeting a gated repository.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: NDJSON stream of tokens, status updates, and completion message

caps.title: Stream Quotes
caps.cap_description: Follow an instrument's quotes live, as its source streams them
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Gives an instrument's quotes as its source streams them. Its input is a live
market-quotes feed ([Market Quotes Feed](https://capdag.com/browse/media:live;market-quotes)):
the selector's `device` names the instrument (`coinbase/BTC-USD`), and the
cartridge that serves this cap opens the source's stream.

## Inputs

- The quotes of a live market-quotes feed.

## Outputs

Market quotes, each as it came, with its feed metadata (`seq`, `pts_us`,
`capture_ts_us`).

## Notes

The feed's selector bounds it: `stop.max_items` or `stop.duration_ms`. Without
one it runs until the run is stopped, and a stop ends it with every quote it
gave. A stream that drops, or a network setting that refuses the source, ends
it as an environment failure.

args.name: quotes
args.arg_description: The quotes of a live market-quotes feed

caps.title: List Compatible Models
caps.cap_description: List locally cached models whose architecture (config.json model_type) is in the supplied set.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Returns the subset of cached models whose detected architecture matches one of the requested architectures. Drives cap-aware model pickers: a cap declares the architectures it can run via `supported_model_types`, the picker forwards that set here, and the user is presented only with usable models.

## Inputs

A JSON record:

```
{ "architectures": ["mistral", "llama", "qwen2"] }
```

## Outputs

A JSON record listing matching models:

```
{
  "architectures": ["mistral", "llama", "qwen2"],
  "models": [
    {
      "model_spec": "hf:org/model",
      "local_path": "/path/to/model",
      "model_type": "mistral"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Notes

- The architecture is read from each cached model's `config.json` `model_type` field. Models without a parseable `config.json` are excluded — a cap that does not recognise an arch cannot load that model.
- The index is in-memory and rebuilt lazily from the cache directory on the first call after process start. Subsequent calls are cheap.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: JSON record { "architectures": ["mistral", "llama", ...] } — the architecture set the calling cap supports.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON record listing matching cached models with local paths and model_type.

caps.title: List Models
caps.cap_description: List all models currently known to modelcartridge.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Returns the authoritative model list maintained by `modelcartridge`, including local models, tracked-but-not-downloaded models, and active downloads.

## Inputs

An optional model repository, a JSON record naming its kind (defaults to `{"kind": "huggingface"}`).

## Outputs

A JSON record with a `models` array. Each model entry carries the same transfer/locality fields exposed by `media:model-status`.

## Notes

- Includes tracked models that are not yet downloaded, as well as active transfers.
- Use [Check Model Availability](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";model-availability;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-availability;record") to check a specific model.
- Use [Download Model](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";download-model;out="media:download-result;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") to add a model to the local cache.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Model repository to list from

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: List of models with their metadata and status

caps.title: Search Models
caps.cap_description: Search the HuggingFace Hub, optionally restricted to a set of architectures.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Searches HuggingFace for models matching a query, with optional restriction to a set of `config.json` `model_type` values. Drives the wizard's first page where the user picks a model — the cap that owns the picker forwards its `supported_model_types` set so search results are pre-filtered to runnable models.

## Inputs

A JSON request:

```
{
  "query": "instruct",
  "limit": 20,
  "tags": [],
  "sort": "trending",
  "cursor": null,
  "architectures": ["mistral", "llama", "qwen2"]
}
```

Optional HuggingFace bearer token (`hf_token`) for gated repositories.

## Outputs

A JSON response:

```
{
  "models": [
    {
      "id": "org/model",
      "model_type": "text-generation",
      "model_arch": "mistral",
      ...
    }
  ],
  "returned_count": 20,
  "has_more": true,
  "next_cursor": "...",
  "previous_cursor": null
}
```

## Notes

- `sort` accepts exactly: `trending`, `downloads`, `likes`, `recent` — anything else is a hard error naming the set (never silently remapped).
- `limit` values above 100 are satisfied by transparent cursor pagination against the HF API (100 per page) — results are never silently capped.

- `model_type` is the HuggingFace pipeline tag; `model_arch` is the structural architecture from `config.json` and is the field used for cap compatibility checks.
- When `architectures` is empty, no architecture restriction is applied.
- Results without a detectable `model_arch` are filtered out when an architecture restriction is in effect — a cap that requires a specific architecture cannot load a model whose architecture is unknown.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Search request JSON record

args.name: hf-token
args.arg_description: HuggingFace bearer token. Required when targeting gated repositories in search.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON record listing matching remote models with detected architecture.

caps.title: Check Model Availability
caps.cap_description: Check if a model is available locally and/or remotely.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Checks whether a model is present in the local cache and/or accessible from its remote repository. Use this before a pipeline that depends on a model to give users a clear message if the model needs to be downloaded first.

## Inputs

A model spec string (e.g. `hf:org/model-name`).

## Outputs

A JSON record with local availability status, remote reachability, local cache path (if present), and file size information.

## Notes

- Does not download the model. Use [Download Model](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";download-model;out="media:download-result;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record") to fetch it.
- For download progress tracking on an already-initiated download, use [Model Status](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";model-status;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-status;record").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Model spec to check availability for

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Model availability information including local and remote status

caps.title: Model Contents
caps.cap_description: List contents of a model repository.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Lists the files inside a model repository along with their sizes, types, and metadata. Useful for inspecting what shards, config files, and tokenizer assets a model contains before deciding which files to download.

## Inputs

A model spec string (e.g. `hf:org/model-name`).

## Outputs

A JSON record with the list of repository files, their sizes, and metadata.

## Notes

- This lists the remote repository contents; it does not require the model to be downloaded locally.
- Use this when building a model spec with `include`/`exclude` filters to understand which files are available to filter on.
- See also: [Check Model Availability](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";model-availability;out="media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-availability;record") and [Download Model](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";download-model;out="media:download-result;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record").

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Model spec to list contents for

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Model contents including files, layers, parameters and metadata

caps.title: Get Model Path
caps.cap_description: Get local filesystem path to a cached model.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Returns the absolute filesystem path to a model that is already in the local cache. Use this when a downstream tool or script needs to reference the model by path rather than by spec.

## Inputs

A model spec string (e.g. `hf:org/model-name`).

## Outputs

A JSON record with the local directory path to the model and a list of files inside it.

## Notes

- Fails if the model is not in the local cache. Download it first with [Download Model](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";download-model;out="media:download-result;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record").
- Useful for integrating with tools that require a filesystem path (e.g. llama.cpp CLI, custom scripts).

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Model spec to get path for

caps.title: Model Status
caps.cap_description: Get the authoritative transfer and locality status for a model.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Returns the authoritative transfer and locality state of a model as maintained by `modelcartridge`. Use this to poll progress during an active download, or to verify whether a tracked model is local, remote-only, failed, or unavailable.

## Inputs

A model spec string (e.g. `hf:org/model-name`).

## Outputs

A single JSON record including state, local/remote availability, byte progress, current file, and any error message.

## Notes

- Poll this cap periodically during a long download to show progress to the user.
- The `state` field is one of `NotDownloaded`, `Downloading`, `Ready`, `Failed`, or `Unavailable`.
- Add an optional HuggingFace token when checking gated repositories.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Model spec to check status for

args.name: hf-token
args.arg_description: Optional HuggingFace bearer token for gated repositories

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: Model status including health, progress and configuration

caps.title: Resolve Model Filters
caps.cap_description: Dry-run a model download to preview which files would be fetched, including any architecture-driven additions on top of the user's filters.
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Resolves a model spec against the remote repository without downloading anything, returning the full effective file list. The response distinguishes the user's include/exclude filter result from the additions modelcartridge would make based on the detected architecture (`config.json` `model_type`).

This is the dry-run companion of [Download Model](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:in="media:enc=utf8;model-spec";download-model;out="media:download-result;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record"). Use it to drive read-only previews in download wizards, where the user's filter is shown alongside the modelcartridge-added mandatory files (e.g. `tokenizer_config.json`, `tokenizer.model`, `special_tokens_map.json`) that are required to load that architecture.

## Inputs

- A model spec string with optional include/exclude filters (e.g. `hf:org/model?include=*.safetensors,*.json&exclude=*-fp32*`).
- Optional HuggingFace bearer token (`hf_token`) for gated repositories.

## Outputs

A JSON record:

```
{
  "model_spec": "hf:org/model?...",
  "applied": {
    "include": ["*.safetensors", "*.json"],
    "exclude": ["*-fp32*"],
    "mandatory_added": ["tokenizer_config.json", "tokenizer.model"],
    "model_type": "mistral",
    "effective_files": [...]
  }
}
```

## Notes

- The resolution result is advisory — the actual download response includes its own `applied_filters` field reflecting the file set used at download time. Compare both to detect repository changes between resolution and download.
- The `mandatory_added` list is empty when the user's filter already covers everything the architecture needs.
- For gated repositories without a valid `hf_token`, the call fails hard with a clear authentication error.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Model spec to resolve filters for

args.name: hf-token
args.arg_description: HuggingFace bearer token. Required when targeting a gated repository.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON record describing the architecture-aware effective file list, including any modelcartridge additions on top of the user's filter.

caps.title: Refine Model Spec
caps.cap_description: Inspect a model spec's repo and derive its canonical model-spec media URN with every detected dim (backend, family, model-task, chat-template, tokenizer-shape, repo-format, quantisation).
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Calls the modelcartridge spec refiner on a single model spec URI. The
refiner inspects the repository's file list and downloads small config
files (`config.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, GGUF metadata ranges) to
derive every dim of the model. The output is a JSON record carrying the
canonical model-spec URI, the narrowed model-spec media URN, and each
detected dim as a discrete field.

The Mac model wizard calls this for every candidate model the user
considers and only surfaces those whose narrowed URN conforms to the
calling cap-arg's required pattern URN. A repo whose dims cannot be
fully detected fails refinement with a hard error rather than a
partial-fill — the wizard's "if we cannot pin down the model, do not
show it" contract relies on every dim being a real detection or
explicit absence.

## Inputs

- A model spec string (e.g. `hf:Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct?include=*.safetensors,*.json`).
- Optional HuggingFace bearer token (`hf_token`) for gated repositories.

## Outputs

A JSON record:

```
{
  "canonical_spec": "hf:Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct?include=*.safetensors,*.json",
  "narrowed_urn": "media:candle;chat-template-jinja;enc=utf8;llm;model-spec;native;qwen;repo-safetensors;tokenizer-unified",
  "repo_format": "safetensors",
  "backend": "candle",
  "family": "qwen",
  "model_task": "llm",
  "chat_template": "jinja-body",
  "tokenizer_shape": "unified-json",
  "quantisation": "native"
}
```

## Notes

- A dim with no detection-evidence is reported as the empty string,
  not omitted — keeps the wire shape stable so the wizard can render
  every dim slot (with "absent" labelling) without per-axis null
  handling.
- The refiner is read-only: no files are downloaded into the model
  cache. The few KB of config it fetches are discarded after
  inspection.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Model spec URI to refine.

args.name: hf-token
args.arg_description: HuggingFace bearer token. Required when targeting a gated repository.

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: JSON record carrying the canonical spec URI, the narrowed model-spec media URN, and each detected dim as a discrete field.

caps.title: Video Frames to PNG Images
caps.cap_description: Deliver a video-frame sequence (live webcam capture or replay) as a standard PNG image sequence
caps.documentation:
## Purpose

Turns a sequence of `media:image;video-frame` items — the CONTENT a
resolved live webcam feed delivers (13.2 §Reference Media) — into the
standard PNG image sequence every image-consuming cap understands. This is
the bridge between live video capture and the rest of the fabric:
`webcam → video-frames-to-png` is the canonical frame-capture machine, the
video analog of `microphone → encode-audio-frames-wav`.

## Inputs

A sequence of `media:image;video-frame` items: individually encoded PNG
frames with `seq`/`pts_us`/`capture_ts_us` per-item metadata and the
capture format actuals (`width`, `height`, `fps`, `pixel_format`) on the
stream metadata.

## Outputs

A sequence of `media:ext=png;image` items — one PNG per delivered frame,
in capture order, per-item metadata preserved.

## Notes

- Items STREAM: each frame is emitted as it arrives (15.2 §Live-Feed
  Machines), so an unbounded feed yields an unbounded PNG sequence — the
  stop condition (or a run stop) bounds it, never buffering.
- Every item is verified to actually be a PNG (magic bytes). A frame
  stream carrying any other encoding is a real input error, not a
  silently mislabeled image.
- Overrun gaps (12.5 §Overrun) are genuine discontinuities: dropped frames
  are simply absent. Nothing is synthesized to paper over loss.
- An empty frame sequence is a real input error, not an empty sequence: a
  feed that delivered nothing means the capture never produced data.

args.name: input
args.arg_description: Sequence of encoded video-frame items (PNG) with capture metadata

outputs.name: output
outputs.output_description: PNG image sequence, one item per delivered frame, capture order

media.title: Aligned Series (JSON, UTF-8, Record, List)
media.description: Several series side by side on the instants they all have: a JSON array of {time, values}.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries series lined up on their shared instants: each item is an instant and the value of every series then, in the order the series were given.

## When to use
Use when several series must be read together, for example before a step that compares them value by value.

## Notes
Instants that any of the series lacks are left out. `values` has one number per input series, in input order.

media.title: API Key (Secret, UTF-8)
media.description: A data source's API key, given for one request.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the key a keyed data source asks for, used for the request it is given with and kept nowhere.

## When to use
Give it to a fetch whose source needs a key (FRED, OpenFIGI and others say so in their profile).

## Notes
The `secret` tag makes interfaces and logs mask it. A source that needs a key and is given none fails with an input error naming the source.

media.title: Astro, Astro Component, Source Code, UTF-8
PCM Audio Frames (Audio)
media.description: Sequence items of raw PCM audio (s16le), each item one capture buffer with pts/seq metadata
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The CONTENT stream of a resolved audio feed: a sequence whose items are raw
PCM buffers (signed 16-bit little-endian). Stream-level metadata carries the
capture format actuals (`sample_rate`, `channels`); every item carries
`seq` (capture-ordered, counting dropped items), `pts_us`, `capture_ts_us`,
and — after an overrun — a `gap` marker (`{dropped, duration_us}`) that
consumers MUST treat as a genuine discontinuity.

## When to use
Declare this as a cap's `in=` (and the arg's `stdin` source) to consume
live or replayed audio at frame granularity. Bounded and unbounded streams
share this type — boundedness is a stream property, not a media property.

media.title: Microphone Feed Reference (Audio)
media.description: Reference to a live microphone capture device (resolved by the runtime into a PCM audio-frame stream)
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A LIVE-FEED REFERENCE (13.2 §Reference Media): the value is not audio data —
it is a small selector record the cartridge runtime (or, on sandboxed
platforms, the host) resolves by opening the microphone and piping an
UNBOUNDED SEQUENCE of `media:audio;audio-frames;pcm` items to the consuming cap's
stdin. The cap is transport-blind: it sees only audio frames.

## Value
A JSON selector record: `device` (provider-defined id; optional when one
device exists), `params` (e.g. `sample_rate`, `channels`), `stop`
(`duration_ms` / `max_items` — absent means "until stopped"), and
`on_overrun` (`drop-oldest` default, or `fail`).

## Notes
An arg declared with this URN must carry a `stdin` source with the audio
content URN and `is_sequence = true`. The feed ends when a stop condition
fires, the run is stopped (close-tap-and-drain), or the run is aborted.

media.title: Background Color (UTF-8)
media.description: Hex RGB matte color (#RRGGBB)
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The matte color that transparent regions composite onto when converting into a format with no alpha channel (e.g. any source with transparency into JPEG).

## When to use
Set on convert-image caps that output JPEG when the source may carry transparency and white (the default) is not the intended backdrop.

## Notes
Strict format: `#RRGGBB` hex (the leading `#` is optional). Anything else is a hard error naming the expected format.

media.title: Bash, Bash Script, Source Code, UTF-8
Batch size for processing (Inference, Limit, Operator, Task, Numeric)
media.description: Batch size for processing

media.title: Batch, Batch Script, Source Code, UTF-8
Benchmark Comparison (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A price path measured against a benchmark on the dates both have: excess return, tracking error, information ratio, beta, correlation, up and down capture.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries how a path did against its benchmark: how much more it returned, how much the difference swings for a year, the difference over its swings, how much it moves with the benchmark, and how much of the benchmark's rises and falls it took part in.

## When to use
Use to judge a fund, a portfolio or an asset against the index it is meant to beat.

## Notes
`information_ratio` is null when the difference never swings; `up_capture` and `down_capture` are null when the benchmark had no rises or no falls. Fractions throughout: 0.02 is 2%.

media.title: Benchmark Series (JSON, UTF-8, Record, List)
media.description: The series a path is measured against, in the time-series shape.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Identifies the benchmark argument of a comparison. What flows into it is a time series; this URN only keeps the argument distinct from the path it is compared with.

## When to use
Bound by name in a machine, as `benchmark=…`, to any time series.

## Notes
Its argument accepts the time-series media; nothing is ever produced as this type.

media.title: C Header Language, C Header, Source Code, UTF-8
C Language, C Source, Source Code, UTF-8
Model Spec (UTF-8, HF safetensors, Candle (Rust safetensors), Embeddings, tokenizer.json)
media.description: Model specification (scheme:identifier string identifying a machine-learning model).
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A model spec is a compact string that uniquely identifies a machine learning model
and tells the system where to find it. The format is `<scheme>:<identifier>` with
an optional query string for filtering (e.g. `hf:org/model-name?include=*Q8_0*`).
The scheme determines which backend or repository resolves the spec.

## Tag axes
The base anchor `model-spec` may be specialised along seven orthogonal axes:

  - **`repo-format`** (`safetensors` / `pytorch-bin`) — the candle-backed
    on-disk file shape. Only set on candle leaves; the `gguf` and `mlx`
    backends carry no separate repo-format tag because the backend value
    fully identifies the on-disk shape (a `.gguf` file IS gguf-backed by
    definition).
  - **`backend`** (`gguf` / `mlx` / `candle`) — which inference engine
    will load the model. Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the tag.
  - **`model-task`** (`llm` / `vision` / `embeddings` / `image-embeddings` /
    `transcription` / `ocr`) — what the model does. Mutually exclusive: one tag
    per spec.
  - **`family`** (~30 values: `mistral`, `llama`, `qwen`, `phi`, `gemma`,
    `falcon`, `olmo`, `smollm3`, `glm`, `chatglm`, `bert`, `clip`, `siglip`,
    `blip`, `whisper`, `moondream`, `voxtral`, …) — the architectural lineage.
    Mutually exclusive.
  - **`chat-template`** (`chat-template-jinja` / `chat-template-short` /
    `chat-template-absent`) — how the model carries its prompt-formatting
    recipe (Jinja body, registered short-name, or none at all).
  - **`tokenizer-shape`** (`tokenizer-unified` / `tokenizer-bpe-pair` /
    `tokenizer-sentencepiece` / `tokenizer-embedded-gguf`) — which on-disk
    tokenizer files the loader will read.
  - **`quantisation`** (~30 values: `q4-k-m`, `q8-0`, `iq4-nl`, `mlx-4bit`,
    `f16`, `bf16`, `native`, …) — bit-width and scheme of the model's weights.

`modelcartridge`'s spec refiner promotes a bare `media:enc=utf8;model-spec`
to its narrowest applicable form by running the detection algorithm in
`docs/model-family-support.md` §6.9 against the on-disk repo (or the HF
API for remote specs). Caps that need to gate dispatch on a particular
axis (e.g. an OCR cap that requires `chat-template-jinja` AND `glm`)
narrow the corresponding `[[anchor.dim]]` in their TOML.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.

    on-disk file shape. Only set on candle leaves; the `gguf` and `mlx`
    backends carry no separate repo-format tag because the backend value
    fully identifies the on-disk shape (a `.gguf` file IS gguf-backed by
    definition).
  - **`backend`** (`gguf` / `mlx` / `candle`) — which inference engine
    will load the model. Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the tag.
  - **`model-task`** (`llm` / `vision` / `embeddings` / `image-embeddings` /
    `transcription` / `ocr`) — what the model does. Mutually exclusive: one tag
    per spec.
  - **`family`** (~30 values: `mistral`, `llama`, `qwen`, `phi`, `gemma`,
    `falcon`, `olmo`, `smollm3`, `glm`, `chatglm`, `bert`, `clip`, `siglip`,
    `blip`, `whisper`, `moondream`, `voxtral`, …) — the architectural lineage.
    Mutually exclusive.
  - **`chat-template`** (`chat-template-jinja` / `chat-template-short` /
    `chat-template-absent`) — how the model carries its prompt-formatting
    recipe (Jinja body, registered short-name, or none at all).
  - **`tokenizer-shape`** (`tokenizer-unified` / `tokenizer-bpe-pair` /
    `tokenizer-sentencepiece` / `tokenizer-embedded-gguf`) — which on-disk
    tokenizer files the loader will read.
  - **`quantisation`** (~30 values: `q4-k-m`, `q8-0`, `iq4-nl`, `mlx-4bit`,
    `f16`, `bf16`, `native`, …) — bit-width and scheme of the model's weights.

`modelcartridge`'s spec refiner promotes a bare `media:enc=utf8;model-spec`
to its narrowest applicable form by running the detection algorithm in
`docs/model-family-support.md` §6.9 against the on-disk repo (or the HF
API for remote specs). Caps that need to gate dispatch on a particular
axis (e.g. an OCR cap that requires `chat-template-jinja` AND `glm`)
narrow the corresponding `[[anchor.dim]]` in their TOML.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.
