media.title: Cap Definition (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Full flattened cap definition as published in the public registry.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The complete flattened cap definition as produced by the registry publisher
(`flattenCapability` in the fabric build pipeline) and stored at
`/caps/<sha256-of-canonical-urn>/<defver>.json` on the public registry host. Consumers
deserialise this JSON object and use it to discover argument shapes,
default values, output media URN, documentation, and any metadata
attached to the cap.

## When to use
Produced by `cap:lookup-cap;fabric` (and any equivalent local-source variants).
Sandboxed cartridges that need to read a cap's `default_value` (e.g. the
default model spec for the cap they implement) consume this media type via a
peer call to a non-sandboxed lookup cap.

## Schema
A JSON object with the fields produced by the registry's flattener
(`cap.schema.json` describes each):

- `urn` — canonical cap URN string (must round-trip through `CapUrn::from_string`).
- `version` — the definition's version under its URN.
- `title`, `aliases`, `cap_description` — what the cap is called and does.
- `documentation` — long-form Markdown about this cap itself.
- `dims` — the dims the cap was built from, each `{dim, value}`, in order; absent
  when it was built from none. What a dim and a value mean is documented with the
  dim, published on its own at `/dims/<sha256-of-name>/<defver>.json`.
- `args` — every argument: `media_urn`, `name`, `required`, `sources` (CLI flag,
  stdin, position), and optionally `accepts`, `arg_description`, `default_value`,
  `is_sequence`, `streaming`, `metadata`.
- `outputs` — every output: `media_urn`, `name`, `output_description`, and
  optionally `optional`, `carries`, `is_sequence`, `streaming`, `metadata`.
- `abstract` — present and true for a generic-input dispatch umbrella.
- `urn_tags` — the URN's tags as an object.
- `in_spec`, `out_spec` — canonical input/output media URNs extracted from the
  cap URN for fast dispatch.
- `in_media_title`, `out_media_title` — denormalised titles for UI display.
- `registered_by` — provenance of the registration, when recorded.
- `metadata` — the cap's own metadata, names to strings, when it declares any.
- `metadata_json` — the cap's JSON metadata, when it declares it.
- `supported_model_types` — the architectures the cap can run, when it says.

## Notes
Field shape is the registry's wire format; consumers MUST treat it as the
single source of truth and MUST NOT carry a parallel copy.

media.title: Cap URN (UTF-8)
media.description: Canonical cap URN string identifying a capability.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A canonical cap URN string of the form `cap:in="<media-urn>";<tag>...;out="<media-urn>"`.
The string MUST be the canonical (alphabetically normalised) serialisation produced
by the cap URN parser; consumers re-parse it through the `CapUrn` type before any
comparison or dispatch decision — a cap URN is a tagged URN, not a string.

## When to use
This media type identifies the input to caps that look up cap definitions, validate
cap URNs, or otherwise consume a cap URN as data. It is **not** the URN of the cap
itself — that is the cap's own identity. Use this only for caps whose data-flow
input is "the URN of some other cap".

## Schema
A UTF-8 string accepted by the `CapUrn::from_string` parser. Values that fail to
parse are rejected at validation time; this surfaces malformed URNs at the boundary
rather than letting them propagate.

media.title: Change How (UTF-8)
media.description: How a change is measured: percent, log or difference.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets how each value is compared with the one so many observations before it.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
`percent` gives 5 for a 5% rise; `log` the natural log of the ratio; `difference` the value less the earlier one.

media.title: Change Over (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: How many observations back a change is measured from.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets the distance of a change: 1 compares each value with the one before, 12 on monthly data compares with a year before.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
A positive whole number. The first so many observations have nothing to compare with and are left out.

media.title: Change Percent (Numeric)
media.description: The change a forecast statement asks about, in percent of the value when it is said.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets the size of the move a trial asks about: 5 asks whether a series ends 5% above where it stood.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
A finite number; negative for falls.

media.title: Chunk Overlap (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: Chunk Overlap numeric value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Defines the number of tokens or characters shared between consecutive chunks when splitting a document. Overlap preserves context at chunk boundaries, reducing the risk of information loss.

## When to use
Use alongside [Chunk Size](https://capdag.com/browse/media:chunk-size;integer;numeric) on any machine that segments documents. A typical overlap is 10–20% of the chunk size. Set to 0 when strict non-overlapping segments are required (e.g., when deduplication is critical).

## Notes
Valid range: 0–500. Overlap must be less than chunk size. Larger overlaps increase index size and redundancy, which can reduce retrieval precision in embedding-based search.

media.title: Chunk Size (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: Chunk Size numeric value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies the maximum number of tokens or characters in a single chunk when splitting documents for processing. Controls the granularity of content segmentation.

## When to use
Set this parameter on chunking or ingestion machines that split large documents before passing them to models with limited context windows. Smaller chunks increase retrieval precision; larger chunks preserve more context per segment.

## Notes
Valid range: 10–2000. Pair with [Chunk Overlap](https://capdag.com/browse/media:chunk-overlap;integer;numeric) to retain context across chunk boundaries, and with [Max Content Length](https://capdag.com/browse/media:integer;max-content-length;numeric) to ensure chunks fit within downstream limits.

Combine Operation (UTF-8)
media.description: How two series are combined at each shared instant: add, subtract, multiply or divide.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets the arithmetic between the left and right series.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
Instants either series lacks are left out; a division by zero leaves that instant out and is counted.

media.title: Company Identifier (UTF-8)
media.description: A company by one of its identifiers: a ticker (`AAPL`), an SEC CIK (`0000320193`) or an LEI.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Names a company for asking its filings, its reported figures or its instruments.

## When to use
Use as the input of the filing and company caps.

## Notes
A ticker is resolved through the SEC's list of tickers; a CIK is used as given; an LEI is read as 20 characters ending in two check digits.

media.title: Comparison (UTF-8)
media.description: How a value is compared with a threshold: above, below, at_least or at_most.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets the comparison a filter keeps values by, or a forecast statement asks.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
`above` and `below` are strict; `at_least` and `at_most` include the threshold.

media.title: Confidence Threshold (Numeric)
media.description: Confidence Threshold numeric value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A probability cutoff below which a machine's output is considered unreliable and should be suppressed, flagged, or sent to a fallback path. Typically used in classification or decision machines.

## When to use
Set a confidence threshold when downstream processes require a minimum certainty level. Results with scores below the threshold can be routed for human review or discarded. A common starting point is 0.7–0.9 for high-precision tasks.

## Notes
Valid range: 0.0–1.0. A threshold of 0.0 accepts all results; 1.0 requires perfect certainty and will suppress most output. Pair with [Decision](https://capdag.com/browse/media:decision;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record) or classification output types that carry probability scores.

media.title: Correlation (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: How closely two series move together on the instants both have: {correlation, n}.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the Pearson correlation of two series' values at their shared instants, and how many instants that was.

## When to use
Use to check whether two series move together before relying on one to say something about the other.

## Notes
Refused with fewer than three shared instants or a series that does not move.

media.title: Country Code (UTF-8)
media.description: An ISO 3166 alpha-2 country code, such as `US` or `DE`.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Names one country by its two-letter code.

## When to use
Use to ask what series sources offer about a country, or to narrow a search to one country.

## Notes
Two capital letters. A code no country has is refused.

media.title: Country Coverage (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: What the catalogue's sources offer about one country, by measure, and which of the measures any economy's picture needs are missing.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes coverage for one country: {code, country, reach, missing, offered, measures}: how far its offers reach (nothing, thin or covered), the essential measures (policy rate, yield, prices, output, labour, exchange rate) none is offered of, how many offers there are, and the offers' references by measure.

## When to use
Use to see how well a country can be followed before building on its data.

## Notes
Offers only: what has been fetched or kept is the business of whoever keeps it.

media.title: Country (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A country of the catalogue: its ISO code, name, and currency.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes one country as the market catalogue knows it.

## When to use
Use to list countries, or to pick the codes to ask coverage or offers for.

## Notes
`code` is ISO 3166 alpha-2; `currency` is the ISO 4217 code of its currency.

media.title: Criterion (UTF-8)
media.description: Free-text intent that frames a semantic judgment or ordering
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The free-text context/intent argument of the semantic-primitive family (`--context` on `same`, and the `--by`/`--for` arguments of the primitives that follow): a short natural-language statement of what the judgment should mean, e.g. "company names on invoices" or "most likely to reply positively".

## When to use
Bind to the context/criterion flag of semantic caps. Keep it one sentence — it configures the transform; it is never a conversation.

media.title: Data Source Id (UTF-8)
media.description: A data source by its id, such as `fred` or `worldbank`.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Names one data source of the market catalogue.

## When to use
Use to describe a source: who publishes it, on what terms, and what it offers.

## Notes
Lowercase letters, digits and '-'.

media.title: Data Source (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A data source's profile: who publishes it, where, its standing, how it is reached, its licence, and the feeds it declares.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes one source of the market catalogue: its id and name, the publisher and their jurisdiction, its standing (official, established or community), whether it needs a key, the homepage and licence terms, and its feeds with what each offers.

## When to use
Use to choose sources, to check their terms before relying on them, or to list what a source can be asked.

## Notes
`jurisdiction` is an ISO 3166 alpha-2 code, or `world` for international bodies.

media.title: Dated Event (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Something that happened, from an events feed: when, what kind, its title, and a link.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes one dated item from an events or news feed: its instant, its kind (such as a release, a decision or a filing), its title, where it can be read and which source said it.

## When to use
Use to follow what sources report about an economy, a market or a company.

## Notes
The instant is RFC 3339 in UTC.

media.title: Decision (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Boolean decision as a JSON object with title, identifier, value, confidence, reason, and threshold-flag fields.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Encodes the result of a binary evaluation as a structured JSON record. `title` carries the human-readable name for the row (used by downstream writers to derive a per-row file name); `identifier` records the question or criterion that was assessed; `value` holds the boolean answer. The record also carries the judgment envelope (docs/semantic-primitives.md, law P2): `confidence` (0.0-1.0), `reason` (one sentence naming the decisive evidence), and `confidence_below_threshold` (whether the confidence fell under the cap's `--confidence-threshold`).

## When to use
Use this type as the output of machines that perform yes/no classification, verification, or filtering. It is the canonical output for [Decision Type](https://capdag.com/browse/media:decision-type;enc=utf8) `binary` and `verification` modes.

## Notes
The schema requires six fields: `title` (string), `identifier` (string), `value` (boolean), `confidence` (number 0-1), `reason` (string), and `confidence_below_threshold` (boolean). No additional properties are allowed. The `title` field is sourced from upstream `StreamMeta.title` provenance for single-decision caps, and from the per-row question for multi-decision caps. For multi-class outputs, consider a classification-specific media type.

media.title: Fabric Defver (UTF-8)
media.description: Per-definition version under a fabric manifest snapshot.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A non-negative integer carrying the per-definition version (defver) of a cap
or media def under a fabric registry manifest snapshot. Encoded as the UTF-8
string representation of the integer.

## When to use
Paired with a `media:cap-urn;enc=utf8` or `media:enc=utf8;media-urn` input
when a caller pins "which version of this URN am I asking for". Absent,
the lookup cartridge resolves the URN's defver under the fabric manifest it
is pinned to; present, the lookup addresses that exact version.

## Semantics
- `>= 1` ⇒ the versioned path (`<kind>/<sha>/<defver>.json`), the only
  path the fabric serves.
- `0` names no version and is rejected as input.

## Schema
A UTF-8 string that parses as a `u32` and represents a positive integer.
Values that fail to parse, or whose value is 0, are rejected.

media.title: UTF-8, Plain Text, Plain Text, Digitized
media.description: Verbatim text digitized from an image by an OCR model. A concrete terminal type — directly persistable as a `.txt` file.
media.documentation:
## Purpose

Carries the verbatim text recognised inside an image by an
optical-character-recognition model. The payload is plain UTF-8 text. The
`digitized-text` marker conveys that the text was *read out of* the image — it
is what the image *contains*, not what the image *depicts*.

## When to use

Use `media:digitized;enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text` as the output type of OCR
caps. The composite URN carries:

- `digitized-text` — the OCR-specific marker so downstream tools that
  specifically want OCR output (indexers, search pipelines, document
  digitisation flows) can match on the more specific type;
- `plain-text` — the finalised-text marker that opts into `save-as-txt`'s
  persistence path;
- `file-type = txt` — binds the URN to the `.txt` extension and `text/plain`
  MIME at the registry level.

## Notes

The text content is unstructured natural language as transcribed by the model.
Some OCR models can be prompted to emit Markdown, HTML tables, or
layout-preserving form; those richer outputs are still UTF-8 text, but if you
need structured representation with bounding boxes or
per-token confidences, define a different media type for that payload shape.

## Distinction from image-description

[Image description](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text)
is a generated caption — a model's prose answer about what an image shows.
Digitized text is the literal characters present in the image. A photograph of
a stop sign yields the *description* "a red octagonal sign on a pole" but the
*digitized text* "STOP".

media.title: Model Download Result (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Result from a model download operation, including the local path and download metadata
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Reports the outcome of a `modelcartridge` download attempt, including the local path when bytes are present, the architecture-aware file filter actually applied, and the refined model-spec profile used by downstream loaders.

## When to use
Return this type from any cap that performs a model download operation. Downstream caps that need the local path to load the model can consume the `path` field directly. For in-progress download state, use [Model Status](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-status;record) instead.

## Notes
`modelcartridge` always emits the same six top-level fields: `success`, `model_spec`, `path`, `error`, `applied_filters`, and `refined`. Failed downloads set `success = false`; `path` may still be present when bytes landed on disk but refinement failed afterwards. `applied_filters` and `refined` are nullable because they are unavailable on early failures.

media.title: Embedding Vector (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Output from embedding generation including vectors, chunk metadata, and model information
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the result of running an embedding model over one or more chunks of text. Each result entry pairs a chunk (text, offsets, index) with its dense floating-point vector, allowing downstream consumers to build indexes, compute similarity, or store vectors without re-running the model.

## When to use
Use this type as the output of any embedding cap. Consumers expecting a list of pre-computed vectors from a single document or batch should accept this type. For multi-document batches see [Embedding Vector List](https://capdag.com/browse/media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;list;record).

## Notes
The `embedding_dim` field on the top-level object must match the length of every `embedding` array in `results`. Implementers should validate this invariant. The `start_offset` and `end_offset` fields are byte offsets into the original source document and can be used to reconstruct which portion of a document each vector covers.

media.title: Model Spec (UTF-8, GGUF (llama.cpp), Embeddings, Embedded in GGUF)
media.description: Model specification (scheme:identifier string identifying a machine-learning model).
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A model spec is a compact string that uniquely identifies a machine learning model
and tells the system where to find it. The format is `<scheme>:<identifier>` with
an optional query string for filtering (e.g. `hf:org/model-name?include=*Q8_0*`).
The scheme determines which backend or repository resolves the spec.

## Tag axes
The base anchor `model-spec` may be specialised along seven orthogonal axes:

  - **`repo-format`** (`safetensors` / `pytorch-bin`) — the candle-backed
    on-disk file shape. Only set on candle leaves; the `gguf` and `mlx`
    backends carry no separate repo-format tag because the backend value
    fully identifies the on-disk shape (a `.gguf` file IS gguf-backed by
    definition).
  - **`backend`** (`gguf` / `mlx` / `candle`) — which inference engine
    will load the model. Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the tag.
  - **`model-task`** (`llm` / `vision` / `embeddings` / `image-embeddings` /
    `transcription` / `ocr`) — what the model does. Mutually exclusive: one tag
    per spec.
  - **`family`** (~30 values: `mistral`, `llama`, `qwen`, `phi`, `gemma`,
    `falcon`, `olmo`, `smollm3`, `glm`, `chatglm`, `bert`, `clip`, `siglip`,
    `blip`, `whisper`, `moondream`, `voxtral`, …) — the architectural lineage.
    Mutually exclusive.
  - **`chat-template`** (`chat-template-jinja` / `chat-template-short` /
    `chat-template-absent`) — how the model carries its prompt-formatting
    recipe (Jinja body, registered short-name, or none at all).
  - **`tokenizer-shape`** (`tokenizer-unified` / `tokenizer-bpe-pair` /
    `tokenizer-sentencepiece` / `tokenizer-embedded-gguf`) — which on-disk
    tokenizer files the loader will read.
  - **`quantisation`** (~30 values: `q4-k-m`, `q8-0`, `iq4-nl`, `mlx-4bit`,
    `f16`, `bf16`, `native`, …) — bit-width and scheme of the model's weights.

`modelcartridge`'s spec refiner promotes a bare `media:enc=utf8;model-spec`
to its narrowest applicable form by running the detection algorithm in
`docs/model-family-support.md` §6.9 against the on-disk repo (or the HF
API for remote specs). Caps that need to gate dispatch on a particular
axis (e.g. an OCR cap that requires `chat-template-jinja` AND `glm`)
narrow the corresponding `[[anchor.dim]]` in their TOML.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.

media.title: Entity Type (UTF-8)
media.description: The kind of real-world entity a value is normalized as (company, person, date, address, unit, phone, ...)
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Names the entity kind for `normalize`: what canonical form the value should take (dates → RFC 3339, phones → E.164, companies → registered name, ...).

## When to use
Bind to `--type` on normalization caps. Free-text by design — the canonical forms for the common kinds are defined in the cap's documentation, and unfamiliar kinds are judged by the model with the confidence reflecting that.

media.title: CSV, CSV, UTF-8, List, Record
media.documentation:
## CSV file

A `.csv` file on disk: the `ext=csv` file-type tag (the on-disk format) plus the
`fmt=csv` content tag (the serialization the bytes are in). A file handler that
reads a `.csv` declares both axes — `ext=` records where the bytes came from,
`fmt=` records how to parse them. Pure CSV *content* flowing between caps (never a
file) carries `fmt=csv` alone (see `_csv-data.toml`).

CSV is by definition a list of records (a header row plus one record per data
row), so both `list` and `record` markers are required.

media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the text of one filing as published: the HTML of its primary document.

## When to use
Use as the input of reading a filing into its sections and financial tables.

## Notes
It is an HTML file, so anything that takes HTML takes it too.

media.title: UTF-8, Plain Text, Plain Text, Image Description
media.description: A vision model's natural-language description of an image. A concrete terminal type — directly persistable as a `.txt` file.
media.documentation:
## Purpose

Carries the natural-language output produced by a vision model when asked to
describe an image. The payload is plain UTF-8 text. The `image-description`
marker conveys that the text is specifically a model-generated caption or
description rather than arbitrary prose.

## When to use

Use `media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;image-description;plain-text` as the output type of
vision inference caps that produce textual descriptions of images. The
composite URN carries:

- `image-description` — the vision-specific marker so downstream tools that
  aggregate or index captions (search pipelines, accessibility metadata)
  can match on the more specific type;
- `plain-text` — the finalised-text marker that opts into `cap:save-as-txt`'s
  persistence path;
- `file-type = txt` — binds the URN to the `.txt` extension and `text/plain`
  MIME at the registry level.

## Notes

The text content is unstructured natural language. If a structured
representation (e.g. tags, bounding boxes) is needed, define a different
media type for that payload shape.

## Distinction from digitized-text

[Digitized text](https://capdag.com/browse/media:digitized;enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text)
is the literal characters present in the image (OCR). Image description is a
generated caption — a model's prose answer about what an image shows. A
photograph of a stop sign yields the *description* "a red octagonal sign on
a pole" but the *digitized text* "STOP".

media.title: Document Page, UTF-8, Plain Text, Plain Text
media.description: A single page of finalised plain text extracted from a multi-page document. Concrete text terminal — directly persistable as a `.txt` file.
media.documentation:
## Purpose

A per-page text payload produced by document-disbinding caps (PDF disbind,
EPUB disbind, etc.). One stream item per page; each item is the full plain
text of that page.

## When to use

`media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;page;plain-text` is the output of `cap:disbind-pdf` and
analogous disbind caps. The composite URN carries:

- `role = page` — the per-page sequence marker (so consumers know each item
  is one page rather than the entire document concatenated);
- `plain-text` — the finalised-text marker that opts into `cap:save-as-txt`'s
  persistence path;
- `file-type = txt` — binds the URN to the `.txt` extension and `text/plain`
  MIME at the registry.

## Notes

The text content is unstructured natural-language text as the disbinder
extracted it. Order is preserved across the stream (page 1, page 2, …).
Each page is its own scalar; consumers that need the whole document as one
blob should aggregate explicitly.

media.title: UTF-8, Plain Text, Plain Text
media.description: Finalised plain text suitable for writing to a `.txt` file. The narrow concrete terminal type for generated or digitized text that is destined for disk persistence.
media.documentation:
## Purpose

Marks a text payload as **finished plain text intended for persistence**. It is
strictly more specific than `media:enc=utf8` (the generic UTF-8 text type) and is the
canonical input/output pair for the `save-as-txt` cap.

The `plain-text` marker exists to keep the planner's path-discovery from treating
every `media:enc=utf8` value as a candidate for `.txt` persistence. Without it, any
text-producing cap (PDF page extractor, JSON adapter, prompt loader) would
appear as a feeder for `save-as-txt`, polluting the recommended-paths surface with
nonsensical chains. The `plain-text` marker forces caps that genuinely produce
user-facing prose (LLM text-generation, OCR's digitized text, etc.) to opt in
explicitly, leaving intermediate text values out of the persistence path.

## When to use

- As `out` on caps that produce user-facing prose ready for disk: LLM
  text-generation caps, document-summarisation caps, code-generation caps.
- As `in` on caps that persist or display finalised text: `save-as-txt` is the
  canonical example.

## When NOT to use

- For intermediate text values that downstream caps will consume (raw page
  text from a PDF, JSON-as-text waiting for parsing, prompt strings). Those stay
  on `media:enc=utf8`.
- For structured text that carries its own format identity (Markdown, JSON, CSV,
  XML). Those use their own concrete file-type markers.

## Notes

- The `file-type = "txt"` narrowing binds this URN to the `.txt` extension and
  `text/plain` MIME type at the registry level — the writer needs no special
  handling beyond the standard extension lookup.
- The payload is UTF-8 text. No structure, no schema, no metadata side-channel.
  Token counts, finish reasons, and the like belong on the streaming-record type
  `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream`; this type is the post-streaming, ready-to-save
  artefact.

media.title: Feed Check (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Whether a series answers now: what it brought, its first and last instants, or why it did not.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Records one check of a series reference: {reference, asked_at, answers, observations, first, last, why}: when it was asked, whether it answers, how many values stand and their first and last instants, and the source's own words when it does not answer.

## When to use
Use to find dead or stale series before a machine relies on them.

## Notes
A source that refuses for want of a key says so, distinct from one that does not answer.

media.title: File Path (UTF-8)
media.description: File Path file system path
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a single file system path as a plain-text string, used to identify the location of an input or output file on disk.

## When to use
Use this type when a machine needs to read from or write to a specific file, rather than receiving content inline. Prefer inline content media types when the file is small and the path adds unnecessary indirection.

## Notes
The path must not contain null bytes. Relative or absolute paths are both valid; the interpretation is determined by the machine's runtime context. A cap that takes several files declares its input as a sequence and receives one path per item.

media.title: Filing Content (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: What a filing says, read: its sections under their headings, its financial tables cell by cell, and every heading in order.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a document read into structure: `sections`, each passage with its heading, text and where it stands; `tables`, each with where it stands, its rows of cells (each cell's text and how many columns and rows it spans) and which rows are headings; `headings`, in document order, including those with no text of their own; and `engine`, the OCR cap that read pages from their pictures, when one did.

## When to use
Use to quote a filing, to find a figure in its tables, or to feed its passages to further reading.

## Notes
Numbers in table cells are kept as written; reading them as figures is left to the consumer. A passage's location says its page in a document that has pages, and `(recognised)` where its page was read from a picture. A PDF's tables are not recovered as tables.

media.title: Filing Form (UTF-8)
media.description: A filing form to keep, such as 10-K, 10-Q or 8-K.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Narrows a listing of filings to one form.

## When to use
Give it to list only annual reports, quarterly reports or current reports.

## Notes
Matched exactly, ignoring case. Amendments carry their own form (10-K/A).

media.title: Filing (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A filing a company made with the SEC: {cik, accession, form, title, filed, report_date, document_url}.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes one filing from EDGAR: the company's CIK, the accession number, the form (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K and others), when it was accepted, the end of the period it reports when it has one, and the address of its primary document when it has one.

## When to use
Use to list a company's filings and pick the ones to read.

## Notes
Times are RFC 3339 in UTC. `document_url` is what fetch-filing fetches; a filing without one has no primary document to fetch.

media.title: Filtered-Out Observations (JSON, UTF-8, Record, List)
media.description: The observations of a series a filter did not keep.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Identifies the second output of filtering a series: what failed the comparison. What flows out of it is the filtered series' own type, unchanged.

## When to use
Take it by name in a machine, as `dropped=…`, to handle what a filter set aside.

## Notes
The output carries the input's type, so it is read as the series that was filtered; nothing is produced as this type itself.

media.title: Forecast Outcomes (JSON, UTF-8, Record, List)
media.description: Forecasts and what came of them: a JSON array of {probability, came_true}.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries settled forecasts of yes-or-no statements: the probability each gave and whether the statement came true.

## When to use
Use as the input to scoring a forecaster's record.

## Notes
`probability` is between 0 and 1 inclusive.

media.title: Forecast Score (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: How good a set of forecasts was: its Brier score, that of saying 50% every time, whether it beats that, and its calibration by tenths.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a forecaster's record scored: the mean squared distance between what was said and what came (lower is better), the 0.25 that saying 50% every time scores, and for each tenth of the scale how many forecasts said about that and how often they came true.

## When to use
Use to tell whether a forecaster, a rule or a model is better than chance and whether its 70% means 70%.

## Notes
`calibration` lists only tenths with forecasts, lowest first; tenth 0 is under 10%, tenth 9 is 90% and over.

media.title: Forecast Trial (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: How ways of forecasting a change in a series, chosen on history, did on history they were not chosen on.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a hindcast: the statement asked at each moment, the ways of forecasting tried, the test stretches with the way chosen on what came before each and how it scored there, the totals over every test stretch against saying 50% every time, and the calibration of the ways as chosen.

## When to use
Use before trusting a rule with a forecast: a rule that only looked good on the history it was chosen on shows here.

## Notes
Scores are in basis points of the Brier score (lower is better; 2500 is saying 50% every time). The first stretch is only learned from, never scored.

media.title: Instrument Identity (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: An instrument an identifier maps to (OpenFIGI): {name, figi, listing, uri}, the listing its ticker and Bloomberg exchange code.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes one instrument an identifier names: its name, its Financial Instrument Global Identifier, and its listing (ticker and exchange code, as `AAPL US`).

## When to use
Use to turn a ticker or another identifier into the instruments it may mean.

## Notes
One identifier often maps to several instruments, one per listing. Exchange codes are Bloomberg's, not MICs.

media.title: Legal Entity (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A legal entity as GLEIF registers it: its LEI, its legal name, and where its record is: {lei, name, uri}.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes one legal entity from the Global LEI Index, as its record names it.

## When to use
Use to confirm who an LEI names.

## Notes
Only an entity whose registration is active is given; an LEI GLEIF does not hold, or whose entity is not active, is refused as an input failure.

media.title: Rate Series (JSON, UTF-8, Record, List)
media.description: A rate earned without risk over time, in the time-series shape.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Identifies the rate argument of excess returns: a yield or policy rate series whose earnings are taken out of a path's returns.

## When to use
Bound by name in a machine, as `rate=…`, to any time series of a rate.

## Notes
Its argument accepts the time-series media; how the rate is written (percent or fraction) is a separate option.

media.title: Regression Residuals (JSON, UTF-8, Record, List)
media.description: What a regression's fit leaves unexplained at each instant, as a time series.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries, for each instant the fit used, the dependent value less the fitted value.

## When to use
Use to look at what a factor does not explain, or to feed the residuals to further series steps.

## Notes
It is a time series, so every series step takes it.

media.title: Regressor Series (JSON, UTF-8, Record, List)
media.description: A series a regression explains another by, in the time-series shape.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Identifies the regressors argument of a regression: one or more series, gathered in the order the machine names them.

## When to use
Bound by name in a machine, once per regressor, as `x=a, x=b`.

## Notes
Its argument accepts the time-series media and takes a sequence; the coefficients come back in the same order.

media.title: Right-Hand Series (JSON, UTF-8, Record, List)
media.description: The second series of a two-series step, in the time-series shape.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Identifies the right-hand argument of a step over two series (combining them, correlating them), keeping it distinct from the left-hand main input.

## When to use
Bound by name in a machine, as `right=…`, to any time series.

## Notes
Its argument accepts the time-series media; nothing is ever produced as this type.

media.title: Time Series (JSON, UTF-8, Record, List)
media.description: A series of dated numbers: a JSON array of {time, value}, oldest first.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries one series of observations: each item is an instant, written as an RFC 3339 date-time in UTC, and the number observed then. A price path, a rate, an economic indicator or a derived series all travel as this.

## When to use
Use as the input and output of steps over series: fetching one, resampling, changing, rolling, combining, regressing, measuring returns. It is a list of JSON records, so the generic record caps (to CSV, to YAML, editing records) also apply to it.

## Notes
Items are in ascending time order with no two at one instant; a producer that cannot guarantee that fails rather than emitting it. Values are finite numbers: a missing observation is left out, never written as null or NaN.

media.title: LLM Generation Request (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Request object for LLM text generation containing prompt, model specification, and generation parameters
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries all inputs needed to invoke an LLM text generation cap: the prompt, the model to use, and any sampling or constraint parameters. A single request object lets callers express the full generation intent without needing multiple input ports.

## When to use
Pass this type to any cap that performs text generation, vocabulary inspection (`get_vocab`), or model information retrieval (`get_info`). For streaming responses the cap should produce a [LLM Text Stream](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;llm-text-stream); for non-streaming responses, use `cap:llm-text-generation-*` which emits [Plain Text](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text).

## Notes
The `request_type` field defaults to `generate` when absent. Constraint fields (`grammar`, `json_schema`, `constraint`) are mutually exclusive in practice; implementers should apply the first one present. The `model_spec` value follows the same format described in [Model Spec](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;model-spec).

media.title: LLM Model Info (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Information about a loaded LLM model including capabilities and parameters
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes a loaded LLM's structural properties and capabilities, including vocabulary size, maximum context length, embedding dimensions, and feature flags such as chat template and tool-use support.

## When to use
Retrieve this type when a cap or orchestrator needs to know model capabilities before issuing a generation request. It is the response to a `get_info` request in a [LLM Generation Request](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-generation-request;record).

## Notes
The `model_spec` and `vocab_size` fields are required. All other fields are optional and may be absent if the model file does not expose the corresponding metadata. Callers should treat missing fields as unknown rather than assuming a default value.

media.title: LLM Vocabulary Response (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Response containing the model's vocabulary tokens
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Returns the full token vocabulary of a loaded LLM, enabling token-level analysis, prompt engineering tools, and custom tokenization utilities to operate without a separate tokenizer library.

## When to use
This is the response to a `get_vocab` request in a [LLM Generation Request](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-generation-request;record). Use it when you need to enumerate, inspect, or count the tokens the model recognises.

## Notes
The `vocab` array is ordered by token ID. The `vocab_size` field should equal the length of `vocab`; include it as a convenience for consumers that only need the count without iterating the full array. Vocabulary extraction is typically slow on large models; cache the result when possible.

media.title: Market Quote (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A live price: last trade, bid and ask, with the instant they stood at.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries one quote of an instrument: the instant the source stamped it with, the last traded price and the best bid and ask where the source gives them, and the unit they are in.

## When to use
Use for the current price of an instrument, one at a time or as a stream.

## Notes
A price the source did not give is null, never zero. A stream's quotes are in the order the source sent them.

media.title: Media Definition (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Full media definition as published in the public registry.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The complete media definition as published by the registry publisher and
stored at `/media/<sha256-of-canonical-urn>/<defver>.json` on the public registry host.
Consumers deserialise this JSON object to read the media type's title,
description, MIME type, documentation, profile URI, file extensions,
validation rules, and metadata.

## When to use
Produced by `cap:lookup-media-def;fabric` (and any equivalent local-source
variants). Sandboxed cartridges that need to inspect a media URN's metadata
without bundling the catalogue into their binary consume this media type via a
peer call to a non-sandboxed lookup cap.

## Schema
A JSON object with the fields produced by the registry's media-def emitter:

- `urn` — canonical media URN string (must round-trip through `MediaUrn::from_string`).
- `title` — human-readable name.
- `description` — short description.
- `media_type` — IANA MIME type, when applicable.
- `profile_uri` — JSON Schema profile URL describing the on-the-wire shape, when applicable.
- `documentation` — long-form Markdown about this media type itself.
- `dims` — the dims the media type was built from, each `{dim, value}`, in order;
  absent when it was built from none. What a dim and a value mean is documented
  with the dim, published on its own at `/dims/<sha256-of-name>/<defver>.json`.
- `extensions` — array of file extensions (without the dot), when applicable.
- `validation` — optional structural validation rules.
- `metadata` — optional registry-specific metadata block.

## Notes
Field shape is the registry's wire format; consumers MUST treat it as the
single source of truth and MUST NOT carry a parallel copy.

media.title: Model Architecture List (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: JSON record carrying a set of `config.json` `model_type` values used to filter cached models by architecture.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the set of architecture identifiers a cap supports (its `supported_model_types`). Used by `list-compatible-models` and similar caps to drive cap-aware model pickers — the user is presented only with models whose detected architecture is in this set.

## When to use
Pass this record from a cap's `supported_model_types` declaration to `cap:list-compatible-models` to retrieve the cached models the cap can run. The same shape is reused by the `architectures` field of `media:model-search-request`.

## Notes
Architecture identifiers are HuggingFace `config.json` `model_type` values (e.g. `mistral`, `llama`, `qwen2`, `phi3`, `gemma2`). They are NOT pipeline tags — `text-generation` is a pipeline tag, not an architecture.

media.title: Model Availability (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Information about a model's availability both locally and in remote repositories
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Answers whether a given model is present on the local filesystem and whether it exists in its source repository. This is the lightweight check a cap can perform before deciding whether to download, load, or surface a model to the user.

## When to use
Use this type as the output of an availability-check cap when you need a simple yes/no answer before committing to a full download or load operation. For richer per-file inventory use [Model Contents](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-contents;record); for download progress use [Model Status](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-status;record).

## Notes
`modelcartridge` emits `model_spec`, `local_available`, `remote_available`, `local_path`, and `size_bytes`. `local_path` and `size_bytes` may be `null` when unknown or inapplicable. This record intentionally omits richer file inventory and download-progress detail.

media.title: Model Contents (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Complete repository structure with all files and directories for a model
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Provides a detailed inventory of all files and directories in a model repository, including sizes, checksums, and local availability. This allows callers to inspect exactly what a model package contains before or after downloading.

## When to use
Use this type when a user or orchestrator needs to understand which files make up a model, verify checksums, or determine which files have already been downloaded. It is the output of a model-contents inspection cap.

## Notes
The `all_files` array is a flat listing of every entry in the repository. The optional `root` object provides the same information as a hierarchy for UIs that need a tree view. The `metadata` object contains repository-level information such as tags or licence identifiers if the repository exposes them.

media.title: Model Delete Result (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Result from deleting or forgetting a tracked model, including the cancellation of any active download
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Reports the outcome of a `modelcartridge` delete operation. Deletion is authoritative: if the target model is downloading, the download is cancelled first, staged/live files are removed, and the tracked status is forgotten.

## When to use
Return this type from caps that delete or forget a tracked model artifact.

## Notes
`success = false` means the model was not removed cleanly. The `error` field carries the exact reason.

media.title: Model Filter Resolution (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Dry-run preview of which files modelcartridge would download for a model spec, including any architecture-driven additions on top of the user's filters.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Output record for `cap:resolve-model-filters`. Surfaces both the user-supplied include/exclude filter and the modelcartridge-added mandatory files (driven by the detected architecture's `config.json` `model_type`) so the wizard UI can show the user exactly what will be downloaded before they commit.

## When to use
As the response of `resolve-model-filters` calls preceding any download. The same shape is also embedded as `applied_filters` in `download-result` records for post-hoc verification.

media.title: Model List (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: List of available models with their metadata and status
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Returns the authoritative list of refined model artifacts known to `modelcartridge`. This includes fully local artifacts, tracked-but-not-downloaded artifacts, and active downloads. Compatibility-filtered listing calls may add an `architectures` field to explain the filter that was applied.

## When to use
Use this type when you need to reconcile or browse the full set of models `modelcartridge` currently knows about. Each listed model already carries the same transfer/locality fields exposed by [Model Status](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-status;record), including the authoritative `refined` identity.

## Notes
The `models` array always contains full model summary objects, never bare strings. `cap:list-compatible-models` may additionally include an `architectures` field on the top-level wrapper to echo the requested compatibility filter.

media.title: Model Path (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Local filesystem path to a model directory
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the resolved local path to a model directory after a model has been downloaded or located on disk. It pairs the filesystem path with the originating model spec for local handoff between caps.

## When to use
Pass this type between caps that download a model and caps that load or inspect it. A download cap produces a [Model Download Result](https://capdag.com/browse/media:download-result;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record); a path-only reference uses this type when no additional download metadata is needed.

## Notes
`modelcartridge` emits only `model_spec` and `path` for this type. Missing models are surfaced as cap errors rather than an `exists = false` record. Use [Model Availability](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;model-availability;record) when you need a non-throwing local/remote check.

media.title: Model Repository (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A model repository, as a JSON record naming its kind (e.g. {"kind": "huggingface"})
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Identifies which external model repository a model spec resolves against. A repository is a JSON record whose required `kind` names the kind of repository; each kind declares the fields it takes. The only kind today is `huggingface`, which takes no other field and resolves model specifications against the HuggingFace Hub API and download infrastructure: `{"kind": "huggingface"}`.

## When to use
Use this type as a parameter when a cap needs to know which registry to query. Most model specs encode the repository in their prefix (e.g. `hf:` for HuggingFace), so this type is primarily useful when the repository must be specified separately from the spec string.

## Notes
A reader refuses a record whose `kind` it does not know, naming the kind, and a field its kind does not declare. A kind that needs credentials names a stored credential by reference; a repository record never carries a secret. See [Model Spec](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;model-spec) for the combined spec format.

media.title: Model Search Request (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: JSON record carrying a remote-model search query, optionally restricted by architecture.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Input record for `cap:search-models`. Drives the wizard's first page: the user enters a query, the calling cap forwards its `supported_model_types` set as `architectures`, and the response is pre-filtered to runnable models.

## When to use
Whenever a cap needs to drive a model-picker UI against a remote repository. Wire the cap's `supported_model_types` into the `architectures` field so the user cannot select an incompatible model.

## Notes
- `architectures` is the structural architecture set (`config.json` `model_type`), not pipeline tags.
- An empty `architectures` array applies no architecture restriction.
- `cursor` carries the pagination state from a previous response's `next_cursor`.

media.title: Model Search Response (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: JSON record carrying remote-model search results with detected architecture per result.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Output record for `cap:search-models`. Carries the result list plus pagination cursors. Each model entry carries both the HuggingFace pipeline tag (`model_type`) and the structural architecture (`model_arch`) — the latter is the field used for cap compatibility checks.

## When to use
Consumed by model-picker UIs to render search results and drive pagination.

media.title: Model Status (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Detailed model status including state, download progress, and health information
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Reports the authoritative transfer and locality state of a refined model artifact as maintained by `modelcartridge`. This includes the artifact's full refined identity, tracked-but-not-downloaded rows, active downloads, ready local models, failed transfers, and artifacts that are no longer available remotely.

## When to use
Poll this type to drive model-management UIs, orchestration, or reconciliation. The `state` field is the primary state machine input; `local_available` and `remote_available` explain whether the model is usable now and/or can still be fetched again.

## Notes
This media type has a single stable record shape. There is no `"unknown"` sentinel and no alternate schema. `state` is one of `NotDownloaded`, `Downloading`, `Ready`, `Failed`, or `Unavailable`. Progress fields are meaningful during `Downloading`; `error_message` is meaningful during `Failed`. `refined` is always present and is the authoritative identity of the tracked artifact.

media.title: Record Program (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A program over JSON records: an ordered list of operations to select, drop, rename, set, filter, map, sort, limit or reverse.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a deterministic transformation of a list of records, written in a closed operation language: `{"ops": [{"op": "filter", "field": "price", "predicate": "gt", "value": 10}, …]}`.

## When to use
Use to reshape records without a model: the program is run exactly as written.

## Notes
Operations: select_fields, drop_fields, rename_field, set_field, filter (eq, ne, gt, lt, ge, le, contains, exists, not_exists), map_field (lowercase, uppercase, trim, to_string, to_number), sort_by (asc, desc), limit, reverse. A program with no operations, or an unknown one, is refused.

media.title: Refined Model Spec (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: Output of the modelcartridge spec refiner: the canonical model-spec URI, the narrowed model-spec media URN with every detected dim, and each dim as a discrete field.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Output record for `cap:refine-model-spec`. Carries every detected
dim of a model so the Mac wizard can (a) verify the candidate's
narrowed URN conforms to the calling cap-arg's required pattern and
(b) display each dim as a discrete chip on the model card without
re-running detection.

## When to use
As the response of `refine-model-spec` calls during model selection.
A wizard should call this for every candidate before surfacing it; a
candidate whose refinement fails or whose narrowed URN does not
conform to the cap-arg pattern must not be shown.

## Shape
```
{
  "canonical_spec": "hf:Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct?include=*.safetensors,*.json",
  "narrowed_urn": "media:candle;chat-template-jinja;enc=utf8;llm;model-spec;native;qwen;repo-safetensors;tokenizer-unified",
  "repo_format": "safetensors",
  "backend": "candle",
  "family": "qwen",
  "model_task": "llm",
  "chat_template": "jinja-body",
  "tokenizer_shape": "unified-json",
  "quantisation": "native"
}
```

A dim with no detection evidence is the empty string, not omitted —
the wire shape is stable so consumers can render every dim slot
without per-axis null handling.

media.title: Regression (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: An ordinary least squares fit of one series on others: intercept, one coefficient per regressor, R², residual standard deviation and observations.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries how much one series moves with one or more others, fitted on the instants they all have: `y = alpha + betas · x`.

## When to use
Use to measure exposure: how much an asset moves with a market, a factor or a rate.

## Notes
`betas` has one coefficient per regressor, in the order the regressors were given. `residual_std` divides by observations less coefficients less one.

media.title: Reported Fact (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A figure a company reported (XBRL company facts), as MarketOS reads it: {predicate, period, value, valid_from, valid_to, filed, location, uri}.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes one reported figure under MarketOS's name for it (such as `fundamentals.revenue`), for the company's fiscal period (`FY2024`, `FY2024Q3`), its value (an amount with its currency, or a quantity with its unit), the span it is valid for, when it became public, and where it was reported (concept, unit, form and accession).

## When to use
Use to follow a company's revenue, earnings or any reported line over time.

## Notes
A figure is given when it is first reported and when a later filing restates it; repeated unchanged as a comparative, it is not given again. Year-to-date spans that are no fiscal period are left out.

media.title: Return Measures (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A price path's returns measured: total return, growth a year, largest drawdown, volatility, Sharpe and Sortino ratios, value at risk and expected shortfall.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the usual measures of how a path performed and how much risk it carried, its returns being the changes from each value to the next.

## When to use
Use to summarise an asset's or a portfolio's history in one record.

## Notes
Fractions throughout: 0.25 is 25%. Measures for a year use the periods-per-year given. A measure a path cannot have (a growth rate through zero, a Sortino ratio with no fall) is null rather than invented.

media.title: Semantic Judgment (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: JSON record carrying a semantic judgment with confidence and rationale
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The shared output envelope of the semantic-primitive cap family (see docs/semantic-primitives.md, law P2). Every judgment-producing cap emits this shape: the cap-specific `result` payload fields (e.g. `same` for the equivalence cap), a `confidence` between 0.0 and 1.0, and a one-sentence `reason` naming the decisive evidence.

## When to use
Consume this media type downstream of judgment caps (`same`, and the primitives that follow it) to route, filter, or threshold on machine judgments without parsing free-form model text — the shape is guaranteed by token-level constrained generation.

## Notes
- A judgment without a confidence and a rationale is an oracle, not a tool; both fields are always present.

media.title: Series Description (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: What a series holds: how many values, its first and last instants and values, mean, standard deviation, least and greatest.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes a series at a glance as one JSON record.

## When to use
Use to check what a fetch brought, or to report a series' range and spread.

## Notes
`sd` is null for a series of one value. A series with no values is refused, not described.

media.title: Series Offer (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: A series a source offers: its reference, the source and feed, what it measures, and whether it needs a key.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Describes one series that can be fetched: the series reference to fetch it by, which source and feed offer it, the measure it is of (such as GDP or a policy rate), its frequency and whether its source needs a key.

## When to use
Use to find the series to fetch for a country or a measure; its `reference` is what fetch-series takes.

## Notes
An offer says what a source declares; whether the series answers now is what checking a feed tells.

media.title: Series Summary (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: One number that sums a series up, and which summary it is: {summary, value}.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a single summary of a series (its last, first, mean, standard deviation, least or greatest value, or how many values it has) with the name of the summary taken.

## When to use
Use where a machine needs one figure from a series.

## Notes
`summary` is one of last, first, mean, stdev, min, max, count.

media.title: Target Set (JSON, UTF-8, Record)
media.description: JSON object mapping route-target names to their contract descriptions
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The dispatch table of the `route` cap: each key is a target name, each value is that target's contract — a one-sentence description of what it handles. The judgment is constrained to the key set; the descriptions are what the model routes BY.

## When to use
Bind to `--targets` on routing caps. 2–64 entries; empty names or descriptions are hard errors (a target without a contract cannot be routed to honestly).

media.title: Transcript (Record, JSON, UTF-8)
media.description: Speech-to-text transcription result

media.title: NDJSON, UTF-8
media.documentation:
## NDJSON (Newline-Delimited JSON)

A list of JSON values, one per line. Each line is parsed independently as
JSON; the file as a whole is a sequence. The most common NDJSON shape is
"newline-delimited JSON objects" — list of records — but list-of-scalars
NDJSON is also valid (a `.jsonl` file of integers, for example).

`list-marker` and `record-marker` are optional on this anchor, mirroring
`_json-data.toml`. The publisher emits four URN variants:

- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson` — a single NDJSON value (degenerate one-line case);
- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;list` — newline-delimited JSON scalars or arrays;
- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;record` — a single NDJSON record (degenerate);
- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;list;record` — the canonical newline-delimited
  JSON-object form.

media.title: NDJSON, UTF-8, List
media.documentation:
## NDJSON (Newline-Delimited JSON)

A list of JSON values, one per line. Each line is parsed independently as
JSON; the file as a whole is a sequence. The most common NDJSON shape is
"newline-delimited JSON objects" — list of records — but list-of-scalars
NDJSON is also valid (a `.jsonl` file of integers, for example).

`list-marker` and `record-marker` are optional on this anchor, mirroring
`_json-data.toml`. The publisher emits four URN variants:

- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson` — a single NDJSON value (degenerate one-line case);
- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;list` — newline-delimited JSON scalars or arrays;
- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;record` — a single NDJSON record (degenerate);
- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;list;record` — the canonical newline-delimited
  JSON-object form.

media.title: NDJSON, UTF-8, List, Record
media.documentation:
## NDJSON (Newline-Delimited JSON)

A list of JSON values, one per line. Each line is parsed independently as
JSON; the file as a whole is a sequence. The most common NDJSON shape is
"newline-delimited JSON objects" — list of records — but list-of-scalars
NDJSON is also valid (a `.jsonl` file of integers, for example).

`list-marker` and `record-marker` are optional on this anchor, mirroring
`_json-data.toml`. The publisher emits four URN variants:

- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson` — a single NDJSON value (degenerate one-line case);
- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;list` — newline-delimited JSON scalars or arrays;
- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;record` — a single NDJSON record (degenerate);
- `media:enc=utf8;fmt=ndjson;list;record` — the canonical newline-delimited
  JSON-object form.

media.title: LLM Text Stream (NDJSON, UTF-8)
media.description: Streaming output from LLM text generation. Each line is a JSON object with a 'type' field (token, status, complete, tool_request, or error).
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Provides incremental LLM output as newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Each line is a self-contained JSON object that consumers can parse and act on as tokens arrive, without waiting for the full response.

## When to use
Use this type for interactive or latency-sensitive applications where displaying tokens as they are generated improves perceived responsiveness. The final `complete` message signals end of stream and carries aggregate statistics. For non-interactive use, prefer the plain-text output produced by `cap:llm-text-generation-*` ([Plain Text](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;ext=txt;plain-text)).

## Notes
The `type` discriminator is required on every message. Consumers must handle all five types: `token` (partial text), `status` (progress update), `complete` (final summary), `tool_request` (the model wants to invoke a tool), and `error` (generation failed). Messages of unknown type should be silently skipped to allow forward compatibility.

media.title: From Date (UTF-8)
media.description: The first date wanted, as YYYY-MM-DD.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets where a fetched series or listing starts.

## When to use
Give it to narrow a fetch to a span.

## Notes
Inclusive. Omitted, the source's own earliest is taken.

media.title: Model Spec (UTF-8, GGUF (llama.cpp), LLM, Embedded in GGUF)
media.description: Model specification (scheme:identifier string identifying a machine-learning model).
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A model spec is a compact string that uniquely identifies a machine learning model
and tells the system where to find it. The format is `<scheme>:<identifier>` with
an optional query string for filtering (e.g. `hf:org/model-name?include=*Q8_0*`).
The scheme determines which backend or repository resolves the spec.

## Tag axes
The base anchor `model-spec` may be specialised along seven orthogonal axes:

  - **`repo-format`** (`safetensors` / `pytorch-bin`) — the candle-backed
    on-disk file shape. Only set on candle leaves; the `gguf` and `mlx`
    backends carry no separate repo-format tag because the backend value
    fully identifies the on-disk shape (a `.gguf` file IS gguf-backed by
    definition).
  - **`backend`** (`gguf` / `mlx` / `candle`) — which inference engine
    will load the model. Backend-agnostic specs simply omit the tag.
  - **`model-task`** (`llm` / `vision` / `embeddings` / `image-embeddings` /
    `transcription` / `ocr`) — what the model does. Mutually exclusive: one tag
    per spec.
  - **`family`** (~30 values: `mistral`, `llama`, `qwen`, `phi`, `gemma`,
    `falcon`, `olmo`, `smollm3`, `glm`, `chatglm`, `bert`, `clip`, `siglip`,
    `blip`, `whisper`, `moondream`, `voxtral`, …) — the architectural lineage.
    Mutually exclusive.
  - **`chat-template`** (`chat-template-jinja` / `chat-template-short` /
    `chat-template-absent`) — how the model carries its prompt-formatting
    recipe (Jinja body, registered short-name, or none at all).
  - **`tokenizer-shape`** (`tokenizer-unified` / `tokenizer-bpe-pair` /
    `tokenizer-sentencepiece` / `tokenizer-embedded-gguf`) — which on-disk
    tokenizer files the loader will read.
  - **`quantisation`** (~30 values: `q4-k-m`, `q8-0`, `iq4-nl`, `mlx-4bit`,
    `f16`, `bf16`, `native`, …) — bit-width and scheme of the model's weights.

`modelcartridge`'s spec refiner promotes a bare `media:enc=utf8;model-spec`
to its narrowest applicable form by running the detection algorithm in
`docs/model-family-support.md` §6.9 against the on-disk repo (or the HF
API for remote specs). Caps that need to gate dispatch on a particular
axis (e.g. an OCR cap that requires `chat-template-jinja` AND `glm`)
narrow the corresponding `[[anchor.dim]]` in their TOML.

## Notes
The validation regex requires the scheme separator colon to be present and forbids
embedded whitespace in the identifier. Strings of up to 512 characters are allowed
to accommodate long query strings.

media.title: HuggingFace Token (Secret, UTF-8)
media.description: Bearer token for the HuggingFace Hub API.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a HuggingFace Hub bearer token between caps. The token is forwarded as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to the HuggingFace API for the call's duration only — no implicit fallback to the `HF_TOKEN` environment variable, no global state.

## When to use
Use this media type for any cap argument that must reach gated HuggingFace repositories (license-protected models such as the `gemma-*` family). Caps that do not provide a token to a gated download fail hard with a clear authentication error.

## Notes
- The `secret` tag instructs UIs and logs to mask the value.
- An empty string is treated as "no token". Pass a non-empty string to authenticate.

media.title: Index Range (UTF-8)
media.description: Index Range value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies a numeric range of indices in the format `N` (single index) or `N-M` (inclusive range from N to M), used to select a subset of items from an ordered collection.

## When to use
Use this type to select pages, lines, chunks, or records by position. Supply `5` to select index 5 only, or `2-7` to select indices 2 through 7 inclusive.

## Notes
Pattern: `^\d+(-\d*)?$`. An open-ended range (e.g., `5-`) means "from index 5 to the end"; the machine must define this behavior. See [Outline Max Depth](https://capdag.com/browse/media:integer;numeric;outline-max-depth) for depth-based selection.

media.title: Model loading (Inference, Policy, Operator, Model, UTF-8)
media.description: How a model's files are brought into memory
media.documentation:
## Purpose
How a cartridge brings a model's weight files into memory before it runs the model.

- `map`: the files are memory-mapped. Nothing is copied, and parts of the model that are never used are never read. Right for a model on a local disk.
- `read`: the files are read into memory whole before the model is used.
- `auto` (the default): `map` for a model on a local disk, `read` for one on a network filesystem (SMB, NFS, AFP, WebDAV).

## Why a network filesystem is read
Pages of a memory-mapped file on an SMB share can stop arriving. On macOS a vision model's load waited inside the kernel while Metal made the mapping resident, and a Candle load waited in a copy out of the mapping, with no data moving, while other models from the same share loaded. Reading the file whole goes through ordinary file reads.

## Notes
Applies to the loaders that can map: GGUF models, and the Candle language and speech models. The Candle loaders for BLIP, CLIP and BERT always read the file whole.

media.title: Instruction (UTF-8)
media.description: A plain-language description of a transformation to perform
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The natural-language input of the `edit` primitive: describe a transformation of structured data the way you would to a chatbot ("keep only active users, lowercase their emails, sort by name"). The instruction is translated into a schema-constrained deterministic program — the model routes on the instruction and the data's STRUCTURE, never on the data itself.

## When to use
Bind to `--instruction` on instruction-driven transform caps. One imperative description; it configures the transform, it is not a conversation.

media.title: Instrument Reference (UTF-8)
media.description: A traded instrument at a quote source, as `coinbase/BTC-USD`.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Names one instrument at one source of live quotes: the source's id, a slash, and the source's own symbol for it.

## When to use
Use as the input of fetching a quote or following a stream of quotes.

## Notes
The source id is lowercase letters, digits and '-'.

media.title: Label Set (UTF-8)
media.description: Comma- or newline-separated closed set of classification labels
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The allowed labels of a closed-set classification (`classify`). The judgment is token-level constrained to this exact set — a label outside it is impossible by construction.

## When to use
Bind to `--labels` on classification caps. 2–64 labels, comma- or newline-separated, no duplicates; violations are hard errors naming the rule.

media.title: Language Code (UTF-8)
media.description: Language code (ISO 639) naming the language of some content
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Names a language by its ISO 639 code: the two-letter ISO 639-1 code where the language has one (`en`, `fr`, `zh`), the three-letter ISO 639-3 code otherwise (`haw`, `yue`). Machines use it to say which language content is in, or which language to produce.

## When to use
Use this type for any argument or value that names a language: the language a transcription is in, the language an answer is written in. A cap that supports only some languages says which in its own documentation and refuses the others when it runs.

## Notes
Lowercase letters only, no region or script subtags (`en`, never `en-US`).

media.title: Legal Entity Identifier (UTF-8)
media.description: A Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442): 20 characters, the last two check digits.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Names one legal entity as GLEIF registers it.

## When to use
Use to look up a legal entity's registered name, jurisdiction and status.

## Notes
Its check digits are verified (ISO 7064 mod 97-10); an identifier that fails them is refused.

media.title: List, UTF-8
media.description: An ordered sequence of UTF-8 strings (media:enc=utf8;list)

media.title: Locale (UTF-8)
media.description: BCP 47 locale tag (e.g. it-IT) that frames locale-dependent interpretation
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Disambiguates locale-dependent values during normalization — `03/04/2026` is March 4 in en-US and April 3 in it-IT.

## When to use
Bind to `--locale` on caps whose interpretation depends on regional conventions. Omit when the value is unambiguous.

media.title: Media URN (UTF-8)
media.description: Canonical media URN string identifying a media def.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A canonical media URN string of the form `media:<tag>;<tag>;...`. The string MUST
be the canonical (alphabetically normalised) serialisation produced by the media
URN parser; consumers re-parse it through the `MediaUrn` type before any
comparison or dispatch decision — a media URN is a tagged URN, not a string.

## When to use
This media type identifies the input to caps that look up media definitions,
validate media URNs, or otherwise consume a media URN as data. It is **not** the
URN of the media def itself. Use this only for caps whose data-flow input is
"the URN of some media def".

## Schema
A UTF-8 string accepted by the `MediaUrn::from_string` parser. Values that fail
to parse are rejected at validation time.
