media.title: PDF Password (Secret, UTF-8)
media.description: Password for opening an encrypted PDF document.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the password of an encrypted PDF between caps. Passed to the PDF engine for the call's duration only — never stored.

## When to use
Use this media type for any cap argument that opens PDFs (render-page-image, disbind, disbind-to-pdf, bind). Without it, an encrypted PDF fails hard with an error naming the `--password` flag; with a wrong password, the error says so explicitly.

## Notes
- The `secret` tag instructs UIs and logs to mask the value.
- An empty string is treated as "no password".

media.title: UTF-8, Plain Text
media.description: Text written to be read, as a value flowing between caps rather than a file (media:enc=utf8;plain-text)
media.documentation:
The value every cap that reads text as language takes: summarizing,
classifying, embedding, prompting a model. Any plain text matches it — a `.txt`
or Markdown file, a document page, digitized text, an image description. Other
formats reach it through a cap that extracts their readable text.

media.title: Prompt (UTF-8)
media.description: Text prompt to guide model generation or analysis.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A prompt is the primary text instruction sent to a model to drive generation or analysis. It defines what the model should produce, ask, or evaluate.

## When to use
Supply a prompt whenever a machine requires user-authored or dynamically constructed instruction text as a distinct input port, separate from the system prompt or base prompt. Prompts are typically short-lived and task-specific.

## Notes
See also [System Prompt](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;system-prompt) for session-level instructions.

media.title: Question Text (UTF-8)
media.description: Text file with one question per line.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A single natural-language question to be answered, evaluated, or routed by a machine. Suitable for Q&A, classification, and decision machines that process one question at a time.

## When to use
Use `media:enc=utf8;question` for single-question inputs. When processing multiple questions in bulk, use the companion `media:enc=utf8;list;question` type, which carries one question per line.

## Notes
Length is constrained to 5–4096 characters. See [Question List](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;list;question) for batch inputs and [Decision](https://capdag.com/browse/media:decision;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record) for the corresponding output type.

media.title: Rate In (UTF-8)
media.description: How a rate series is written: percent (5.2 for 5.2% a year) or fraction (0.052).
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Says how to read the values of a rate series.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
Most sources publish yields in percent.

media.title: Resample Aggregate (UTF-8)
media.description: How a period's observations become its one value: last, mean or sum.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets how the observations in one resampled period are combined.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
`last` suits prices and levels, `sum` flows such as volumes, `mean` rates averaged over the period.

media.title: Resample Every (UTF-8)
media.description: How often a resampled series has a value: daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly or annual.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets the calendar period a series is resampled to: each period that has observations gets one value, stamped at the period's last observation.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
Periods are calendar periods in UTC: weeks end on Sunday, quarters end in March, June, September and December.

media.title: Rolling Statistic Kind (UTF-8)
media.description: Which rolling statistic: mean, sd, zscore or vol.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets what a rolling step computes over each window.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
`zscore` is the last value of the window less the window's mean, over its standard deviation. `vol` is the window's standard deviation scaled to a year by the periods-per-year given with it.

media.title: Rubric (UTF-8)
media.description: Rubric or requirements text a judgment is made against
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The criteria text of criterion-referenced judgments: the rubric `score` scores against, and the requirements `verify` checks an artifact against.

## When to use
Bind to `--rubric` (score) / `--against` (verify). Judgments are made strictly against this text, not against general quality — write the criteria you actually want enforced.

media.title: Scale (UTF-8)
media.description: Integer scoring scale of the form min..max (e.g. 0..10)
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The integer range a `score` judgment is constrained to. `min..max` with min < max; the emitted score cannot leave the range (token-level constraint).

## When to use
Bind to `--scale` on scoring caps. Malformed scales are hard errors naming the grammar.

media.title: Search Words (UTF-8)
media.description: Words to find something by: data sources, series or countries.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the words a search matches against names, publishers and descriptions.

## When to use
Use to narrow a listing of sources, countries or series offers.

## Notes
Matching ignores case. Empty words match everything.

media.title: SEC Contact (UTF-8)
media.description: Who is asking SEC EDGAR: a name and an email address, sent with every request to it.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The SEC asks everyone who reads EDGAR to say who they are, with a contact address, on each request (its fair access policy). This is that contact.

## When to use
It is a setting: set it once, as a name and an email address such as `Jane Doe jane@example.com`, and every cap that reads EDGAR sends it.

## Notes
Empty until it is set. A cap that reads EDGAR while it is empty is refused with an input error naming this setting, and nothing is sent to the SEC.

media.title: Second Item (UTF-8)
media.description: The second of two items a comparison cap judges
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries the second operand of a two-item comparison cap (e.g. `same`). The first operand arrives as the cap's primary input; this media type disambiguates the second.

## When to use
Bind to the second positional argument (or `--right` flag) of comparison caps.

media.title: Separator, UTF-8
media.description: String inserted between adjacent items when concatenating a sequence
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The infix string a concatenation cap places between adjacent items. Used by [Concat Text](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:concat;in="media:enc=utf8";out="media:enc=utf8") to glue a sequence of text items into a single text value.

## When to use
Pass any UTF-8 string. The cap inserts the value between adjacent items only — never as a leading or trailing prefix on the merged output. Omit the argument for the cap's default separator (newline).

## Notes
Multi-byte UTF-8 separators are supported verbatim; the cap does not split or normalise them. An empty separator butts items directly together without any infix.

media.title: Series Field (UTF-8)
media.description: Which field of a source's answer to take as the series' value, where it gives several.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Picks one column of a source that answers several per instant, such as `close` or `volume` of a price history.

## When to use
Give it to a fetch whose source answers several fields; the source's profile lists them.

## Notes
A field the source does not give is refused with the fields it does.

media.title: Series Reference (UTF-8)
media.description: Where a series comes from: a source and what to ask it, as `fred/UNRATE` or `worldbank/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD?country=US`.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Names one series of one data source: the source's id, a slash, and the source's own name for the series, with any parameters it takes as a query.

## When to use
Use as the input of fetching or checking a series. A machine can give it as a constant, or take it from a search for series.

## Notes
The source id is lowercase letters, digits and '-'. What follows the slash is the source's own identifier, passed on as given.

media.title: Statement Window (UTF-8)
media.description: When a forecast statement must hold: at_deadline or any_time.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets whether a statement is judged on the last value by its deadline or holds once it is ever seen to hold before then.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
`any_time` statements come true more often than `at_deadline` ones of the same size.

media.title: Summary Kind (UTF-8)
media.description: Which summary of a series: last, first, mean, stdev, min, max or count.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets which single number a series is summed up as.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
`stdev` is the sample standard deviation and needs two values.

media.title: System Prompt (UTF-8)
media.description: System Prompt value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The system prompt establishes the model's persona, constraints, and operational rules for a session. It is injected before user messages and is not typically visible to end users.

## When to use
Use this media type when a machine port accepts a session-level instruction block that governs all subsequent turns.

## Notes
Maximum length is 8192 characters. Changes to the system prompt affect the entire session, so treat it as a high-trust input. See [Prompt](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;prompt) for per-request instructions.

media.title: To Date (UTF-8)
media.description: The last date wanted, as YYYY-MM-DD.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets where a fetched series or listing ends.

## When to use
Give it to narrow a fetch to a span.

## Notes
Inclusive. Omitted, the latest the source has is taken.

media.title: Every Days (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: How many days between one moment of a trial and the next.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets how often through history the statement is asked.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
A whole number of days, at least 1.

media.title: Frames Per Second (Numeric)
media.description: Target frame rate for video frame extraction
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies a target frame rate (frames per second) for caps that decimate or sample video frames. The cap selects approximately `fps` frames per second from the source by emitting the first decoded frame whose presentation timestamp passes each `1/fps`-second boundary.

## When to use
Pass to [Extract Frames](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:extract-frames;in=media:video;out="media:ext=png;image") (and its per-container variants) to subsample video into a manageable image stream. With no `--fps` argument the cap emits every decoded frame; with `--fps 1` the cap emits ~1 frame per second.

## Notes
Must be a positive finite number. Caps reject zero, negative, or non-finite values loudly rather than silently passing through every frame, since `--fps 0` is unambiguously a programmer error.

media.title: Horizon Days (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: How many days ahead each forecast looks.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets how far ahead each statement of a trial is judged.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
A whole number of days, at least 1.

media.title: Webcam Feed Reference (Image)
media.description: Reference to a live camera capture device (resolved by the runtime into a video-frame stream)
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A LIVE-FEED REFERENCE (13.2 §Reference Media): the value is not video data —
it is a small selector record the cartridge runtime (or, on sandboxed
platforms, the host) resolves by opening the camera and piping an UNBOUNDED
SEQUENCE of `media:image;video-frame` items to the consuming cap's stdin.
The cap is transport-blind: it sees only frames.

## Value
A JSON selector record: `device` (provider-defined id; optional when one
device exists), `params` (e.g. `width`, `height`, `fps`), `stop`
(`duration_ms` / `max_items` — absent means "until stopped"), and
`on_overrun` (`drop-oldest` default, or `fail`).

## Notes
An arg declared with this URN must carry a `stdin` source with the frame
content URN and `is_sequence = true`. The feed ends when a stop condition
fires, the run is stopped (close-tap-and-drain), or the run is aborted.

media.title: Video Frames (Image)
media.description: Sequence items of encoded video frames (one image per item) with pts/seq metadata
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The CONTENT stream of a resolved camera feed (and of frame-extraction caps):
a sequence whose items are individually encoded frames. Stream-level
metadata carries the capture format actuals (`width`, `height`, `fps`,
`pixel_format`); every item carries `seq` (capture-ordered, counting
dropped items), `pts_us`, `capture_ts_us`, and — after an overrun — a
`gap` marker (`{dropped, duration_us}`) that consumers MUST treat as a
genuine discontinuity.

## When to use
Declare this as a cap's `in=` (and the arg's `stdin` source) to consume
video at frame granularity — a per-frame filter is a ForEach over this
sequence. Bounded and unbounded streams share this type.

media.title: Maximum context length (Inference, Limit, Operator, Model, Numeric)
media.description: Maximum context length

media.title: Maximum tokens to generate (Inference, Limit, User, Task, Numeric)
media.description: Maximum tokens to generate

media.title: Minimum probability sampling parameter (Inference, Sampling, User, Task, Numeric)
media.description: Minimum probability sampling parameter

media.title: RoPE frequency base (Inference, Policy, Operator, Model, Numeric)
media.description: RoPE frequency base

media.title: RoPE frequency scale parameter (Inference, Policy, Operator, Model, Numeric)
media.description: RoPE frequency scale parameter

media.title: Repetition penalty for token sampling (Inference, Sampling, User, Task, Numeric)
media.description: Repetition penalty for token sampling

media.title: Random seed for reproducible sampling (Inference, Sampling, User, Task, Numeric)
media.description: Random seed for reproducible sampling

media.title: Sampling temperature (Inference, Sampling, User, Task, Numeric)
media.description: Sampling temperature

media.title: Top-k sampling parameter (Inference, Sampling, User, Task, Numeric)
media.description: Top-k sampling parameter

media.title: Top-p (nucleus) sampling parameter (Inference, Sampling, User, Task, Numeric)
media.description: Top-p (nucleus) sampling parameter

media.title: JPEG Quality (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: JPEG encode quality (1-100)
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Controls the JPEG encoder's quality/size trade-off when producing JPEG output.

## When to use
Set on convert-image caps that output JPEG. Higher values preserve more detail at larger file sizes; 85 (the cap default) is a good archival-preview balance.

## Notes
Valid range: 1-100.

media.title: Keep Every (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: Stride for sequence decimation: keep one item out of every N
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Stride parameter for the [Decimate Sequence](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:decimate-sequence;effect=none) cap. The decimator keeps items at positions `0, N, 2N, …` of the input sequence and drops the rest.

## When to use
Use to subsample a long sequence — every Nth frame from a video disbinder, every Nth record from a CSV, every Nth file from a folder. With `N = 1` (or no value), the sequence passes through unchanged.

## Notes
Must be a positive integer. Negative, zero, or non-integer values fail loudly rather than being silently treated as 1, so a misspelled flag does not silently disable decimation.

media.title: Lag By (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: How many observations a series is moved later by.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets how far a lagged series is shifted: each instant takes the value of the observation so many before it.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
A positive whole number. The first so many instants have no earlier value and are left out.

media.title: Integer, List, Numeric
media.description: Numeric primitive (integer or real) optionally as a list

media.title: Max Content Length (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: Max Content Length numeric value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Limits the number of characters or tokens of document content passed to a machine. Used to prevent oversized inputs from exceeding downstream capacity.

## When to use
Apply this parameter on ingestion or preprocessing machines that must truncate or split content before forwarding it. It complements [Max Context Length](https://capdag.com/browse/media:inference;limit;max-context-length;model;numeric;operator), which governs the model's total window.

## Notes
Valid range: 256–131072. Content exceeding this limit should be chunked using [Chunk Size](https://capdag.com/browse/media:chunk-size;integer;numeric) rather than silently truncated.

media.title: Model Dimensionality (Integer, Numeric)
media.description: Dimensionality of a machine learning model (e.g., embedding vector size)
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Carries a single integer that describes the output dimensionality of a model, most commonly the size of its embedding vectors. This allows caps to advertise or negotiate the dimension of their output without needing a full model-info record.

## When to use
Use this type as a lightweight parameter or output when only the vector dimension is needed — for example, to size a vector database index or validate that an embedding model's output matches a downstream consumer's expected dimension.

## Notes
The minimum value is 1. Typical embedding models produce dimensions between 128 and 4096. The value should match the `embedding_dim` field in [LLM Model Info](https://capdag.com/browse/media:enc=utf8;fmt=json;llm-model-info;record) or the `embedding_dim` field in [Embedding Vector](https://capdag.com/browse/media:embedding-vector;enc=utf8;fmt=json;record) for the same model.

media.title: Integer, Numeric
media.description: Numeric primitive (integer or real) optionally as a list

media.title: Page Image Height (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: Page Image Height numeric value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies the pixel height to use when rendering a document page as an image. Controls the vertical resolution of the rasterized output.

## When to use
Set this parameter alongside [Page Image Width](https://capdag.com/browse/media:integer;numeric;page-image-width) when you need to control the full resolution of rendered pages. Increasing height improves vertical detail for tall or portrait-oriented documents.

## Notes
Valid range: 50–4000 pixels. Aspect ratio handling is machine-specific. For most document types, setting only width and allowing the machine to infer height is simpler and avoids distortion.

media.title: Page Image Width (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: Page Image Width numeric value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Specifies the pixel width to use when rendering a document page as an image. Controls the horizontal resolution of the rasterized output.

## When to use
Set this parameter on page-rendering or PDF-to-image machines when the default resolution is too low for OCR or visual analysis, or too high for bandwidth-constrained pipelines.

## Notes
Valid range: 50–4000 pixels. Pair with [Page Image Height](https://capdag.com/browse/media:integer;numeric;page-image-height) to set both dimensions. Aspect ratio enforcement is machine-specific; some machines may adjust one dimension to preserve proportions.

media.title: Rolling Window (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: How many observations a rolling statistic is taken over.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets the window of a rolling statistic: each value is the statistic of that many observations ending there.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
A whole number of at least 2. The first window less one observations have no full window and are left out.

media.title: Seed (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: Seed numeric value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
An unsigned integer used to initialize the random number generator, making model outputs reproducible across runs when all other parameters are held constant.

## When to use
Supply a seed when you need deterministic output for testing, debugging, or auditing. Leave it unset in production when varied outputs are desirable.

## Notes
Valid range: 0–4294967295 (32-bit unsigned). Reproducibility depends on the runtime and hardware; results may differ across framework versions or GPU configurations even with the same seed. See [Sampling Seed](https://capdag.com/browse/media:inference;numeric;sampling;sampling-seed;task;user) for the inference-specific variant with richer metadata.

media.title: Stretches (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: Into how many test stretches a trial cuts its moments.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets how many times a way is chosen on what came before and scored on what came next.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
A whole number, at least 2: the first stretch is only learned from.

media.title: Word Budget (Numeric, Integer)
media.description: Maximum length of a produced text, in words
media.documentation:
## Purpose
An upper bound on the length of generated prose (e.g. a summary), expressed in words because that is how humans budget reading.

## When to use
Bind to `--budget` on compression caps. Positive integer; 0 or non-numeric values are hard errors.

media.title: List, Numeric
media.description: Numeric primitive (integer or real) optionally as a list

media.title: List, Record
media.description: An ordered sequence of record-shaped values

media.title: Market Quotes Feed
media.description: Reference to an instrument's live quote stream (resolved by the market cartridge into a sequence of market quotes)
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A LIVE-FEED REFERENCE of a family the market cartridge resolves itself: the
value is a selector record, and the cartridge opens the instrument's quote
stream at its source and pipes each quote, as a market-quote record, to the
consuming cap's stdin.

## Value
A JSON selector record: `device` names the instrument (`coinbase/BTC-USD`, or
`<source>/<symbol>` of a source that declares a stream), `stop` (`duration_ms`
/ `max_items`, absent means "until stopped") and `on_overrun`.

## Notes
The feed reaches its source, so the host's network setting applies to it: a
setting that refuses the source ends the feed as an environment failure. A
stop ends it with every quote it gave.

media.title: Numeric
media.description: Numeric primitive (integer or real) optionally as a list

media.title: Periods Per Year (Numeric)
media.description: How many observations a year holds: 252 for trading days, 365 for every day, 52 weekly, 12 monthly, 4 quarterly.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets how measures for a year (volatility, Sharpe and Sortino ratios, tracking error) are scaled from per-observation figures.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
Positive. It is the series' own frequency, not the calendar: crypto trades every day, 365; equities about 252.

media.title: Repetition Penalty (Numeric)
media.description: Repetition Penalty numeric value
media.documentation:
## Purpose
A lightweight repetition penalty parameter for machines that apply token-level discouragement of repeated output without full inference metadata.

## When to use
Use this type when connecting a simple numeric penalty value to a machine that does not require override-level controls. For full inference configuration, prefer [Repeat Penalty](https://capdag.com/browse/media:inference;numeric;repeat-penalty;sampling;task;user), which includes metadata and override scope.

## Notes
Minimum value is 1.0 (no penalty). No upper bound is defined in this spec; check the target machine's documentation for practical limits. Values significantly above 1.5 risk degrading output coherence.

media.title: Risk-Free Rate (Numeric)
media.description: The rate a year earned without risk, as a fraction, that Sharpe and Sortino ratios measure against.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets the return a Sharpe or Sortino ratio is measured in excess of.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
A fraction: 0.04 is 4% a year. 0 measures against nothing earned.

media.title: Threshold (Numeric)
media.description: The number a comparison is made against.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
Sets the value a filter compares each observation with.

## When to use
Give it as an option of the step that names it.

## Notes
Any finite number.

media.title: Record
media.description: Any value with key-value record structure

media.title: Video
media.description: A video, regardless of container format. The bare `media:video` URN matches any video file (mp4, mov, mkv, webm, etc.); format-specific variants like `media:ext=mp4;video` refine it.
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The umbrella media URN for video content. The abstract [Extract Frames](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:extract-frames;in=media:video;out="media:ext=png;image") and [Extract Audio Track](https://capdag.com/browse/cap:extract-audio-track;in=media:video;out=media:audio) caps take this type; the planner subsumes more-specific format URNs (`media:ext=mp4;video`, `media:ext=mov;video`, `media:ext=mkv;video`, `media:ext=webm;video`) under it.

## When to use
Use `media:video` when authoring a cap that should accept any supported video container without committing to a specific format. For format-aware pipelines, prefer the per-container URNs so the planner can route correctly without ambiguity.

## Notes
Format-specific variants are produced by the `_video-file.toml` template (one entry per file-type × medium=video). The bare `media:video` URN exists alongside them so caps written against the umbrella have a media def to anchor to.

media.title: Void Value
media.description: No value / void return type
media.documentation:
## Purpose
The [Void Value](https://capdag.com/browse/media:void) media type represents the absence of a value — analogous to `void` in programming languages or `null` in type theory. It is used to type ports or outputs that carry no data payload.

## When to use
Use this type for node outputs that signal completion or success without returning any data — for example, a side-effectful node that writes to a database and has nothing to return, or a terminal sink node. It is also appropriate as the type of an optional input port whose absence is meaningful.

## Notes
A void value produces no bytes; its byte length is always zero. Implementers should not transmit any payload when producing a void value, and consumers should ignore any payload bytes if present. This type is intentionally distinct from an empty byte sequence (`media:`) to make the semantic "no output" explicit in the graph schema.
